paragraphs: Within the next two weeks, NFL teams will put the final touches on initial 53-man rosters. In addition to cuts before the August 30 deadline, we'll also see notable trades.
Due to offseason acquisitions and coaching staff changes, some veterans are no longer a fit with their current clubs.

With only a couple of preseason games left to showcase players on the roster bubble, coaches can either give them opportunities to play or hold them out to avoid an injury that could derail a potential trade.
Here's a short list of players to keep tabs on in exhibition games or in the rumor mill, with a probability meter on whether they will be traded before the roster cuts deadline.
Kayshon Boutte, WR, New England Patriots

In 2025, Kayshon Boutte showcased his explosive playmaking ability, hauling in 33 passes for 551 yards and six touchdowns while on the field for 67 percent of the offensive snaps. He's unlikely to top those numbers in New England this year.

The Patriots signed Romeo Doubs and then acquired A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles. So, at best, Boutte will be the No. 3 receiver, and that's not a guarantee. Mack Hollins saw 19 more targets than him last season (65-46), and DeMario Douglas saw the same number of targets. Also, keep in mind that tight end Hunter Henry finished second on the team with 87.

If Boutte wants to significantly raise his market value before a 2027 free-agency bid, he has a much better chance of doing so on another team. The Patriots' receiver acquisitions have pushed him further down the depth chart, making it difficult for him to shine in a defined role.

At 24 and coming off a solid campaign, Boutte should garner interest on the trade block. Former Patriots personnel executive and current Houston Texans general manager Nick Caserio may explore the market for a receiver after losing Jayden Higgins for the season because of a torn ACL.
This offseason, the Kansas City Chiefs turned over their cornerback group and brought back a familiar face.

The Chiefs traded Trent McDuffie to the Los Angeles Rams, and Jaylen Watson signed with the same team in free agency. L'Jarius Sneed signed up for his second stint in Kansas City. The team traded up to the sixth spot in the draft for LSU product Mansoor Delane.

If healthy, Delane is a lead cornerback. Nohl Williams started in five out of 17 contests last season and may have untapped potential as a third-rounder from the 2025 draft. Sneed has four years of experience in defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's system.

Because of injuries, Fulton missed nine outings last year. He didn't crack the starting lineup until the last two games of the campaign. With the changes at his position, the seventh-year pro is likely No. 4 on the depth chart among boundary defenders.
The Chiefs should shop Fulton, who's entering his age-28 season. He could fetch late-round draft capital from a club in need of veteran insurance or a part-time starting cornerback.
However, because of Fulton's limited action last year, teams may be patient to see if the Chiefs cut him by August 30.
A year after the Dallas Cowboys traded three-time first-team All-Pro pass-rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers, they have a crowded room of outside linebackers.

Although no one on the roster compares to Parsons, the Cowboys may not have room for Marist Liufau, who's transitioned from inside linebacker to outside linebacker under new defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

Initially, Liufau had a chance to hang on to a back-end roster spot as he learns a new position, but the Cowboys signed proven pass-rusher Von Miller, who led the Washington Commanders with nine sacks last year.
Miller, Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, rookie first-rounder Malachi Lawrence, Sam Williams and James Houston are ahead of Marist on the depth chart.

Unless Dallas parts ways with Houston or Williams, Liufau is a long shot to make the roster and could draw interest from teams intrigued by his versatile skill set. Otherwise, he's a prime cut candidate.

The Minnesota Vikings named Kyler Murray their starting quarterback before the team's preseason opener. Head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters that J.J. McCarthy has a future with the organization.
McCarthy's future in Minnesota may be cut short by a decent trade offer, though.

The Vikings started McCarthy for only 10 games before they signed Murray. The young signal-caller struggled through his first year as a full-time starter, throwing for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions with a 57.6 percent completion rate, but he's only 23 and has a first-round pedigree.

Typically, the league is generous to quarterbacks who were Day 1 draft picks, given they show some potential. Minnesota went 6-4 in McCarthy's starts, and he had an impressive fourth-quarter comeback and game-winning drive in his regular-season debut.

Given Murray's injury history, the Vikings need a capable backup. So, the front office isn't likely to give McCarthy away for a late-round pick. Teams would likely need to give up a middle-round pick for Minnesota to consider a deal, which is too high a price for a project player in his early stages of development.
Anthony Richardson, QB, Indianapolis Colts
Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones didn't play in the team's preseason opener, but he's been a full participant at training camp practices.
ESPN's Ben Solak attended camp and noted that Jones "looks good."
"I saw an unimpeded Daniel Jones," Solak wrote. "If you didn't tell me the QB was only 7½ months removed from Achilles surgery, I wouldn't have known."

Even though the Colts' QB1 is on track to play in Week 1, assistant general manager Ed Dodds wants to keep three capable signal-callers, which means Anthony Richardson may remain in Indianapolis for at least another year.
"We want to have three [quarterbacks] that can play," Dodds said via ESPN's Stephen Holder . "So, if [Richardson] is one of them, he's going to be here. ... Look at last year. You never know."
In 2025, the Colts started three different quarterbacks: Jones, Riley Leonard and Philip Rivers. Richardson fell out of the rotation with an eye injury.

Still, Rivers probably isn't going to answer the call to play again at 44 years old. Although Richardson has struggled mightily under center, throwing for 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions with a 50.6 percent completion rate in 17 games, he can fill in for short stretches if necessary.
Remember, Jones has an extensive injury history. Aside from 2022 and 2024, when the New York Giants benched him, he's missed multiple games in every other season since 2019.

Also, the Colts may hold on to Richardson because they probably won't receive strong offers for a struggling player who's missed significant time with injuries and played just 14 offensive snaps last year.

The Arizona Cardinals are in a weird spot with Josh Sweat. They placed him on the physically unable to perform list because of a knee injury after he skipped organized team activities and then attended mandatory minicamp without participation .
According to ESPN's Dan Graziano , Sweat told the team he's unhappy.
General manager Monti Ossenfort dodged a question about Sweat's rumored trade request and said the team isn't interested in moving him.

"There is always a lot of talk around that. We have no interest in trading Josh. Some of those discussions we will keep private," Ossenfort said via Darren Urban of the team's official website. "We are excited to have Josh here."

NFL analysts (including this one) expect the Cardinals to finish with one of the league's worst records this year. Journeyman Jacoby Brissett is the starting quarterback, and promising rookie first-round running back Jeremiyah Love is dealing with a high-ankle sprain.
In his age-28 season, Sweat logged a career-high 12 sacks, but the Cardinals are unlikely to contend this season. If Ossenfort doesn't trade him before Week 1, he's just delaying the inevitable.
Kayvon Thibodeaux, Edge, New York Giants
Back in April, The Athletic's Ian O'Connor reported that the New York Giants wanted a second-round pick for Kayvon Thibodeaux.
Fellow scribe from The Athletic, Dan Duggan , heard that the New Orleans Saints were most interested in acquiring Thibodeaux, though general manager Joe Schoen denied those rumors.

Since then, a few teams that may have been interested in Thibodeaux have filled their pass-rushing needs. New Orleans has re-signed Cameron Jordan. The Atlanta Falcons signed Za'Darius Smith. The Chicago Bears added Marcus Davenport.

Productive pass-rushers will always be in demand, but Thibodeaux has seen a significant drop-off in sacks and pressures since his standout 2023 campaign. Furthermore, over the last two seasons, he's missed 12 games because of injuries.

Last year, Big Blue selected edge-rusher Abdul Carter with the No. 3 overall pick. This offseason, with the No. 5 pick, they drafted Arvell Reese, who showed the ability to rush the passer in his last year at Ohio State, logging 6.5 sacks.

Even with the added pass-rushing talent on the roster, Thibodeaux will likely remain in New York past the roster cuts deadline. The Giants' reported asking price is way too high for a player whose production has declined over the past two seasons.
In this year's draft, the Cleveland Browns selected wideouts KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston in the first and second rounds, respectively. Both have flashed this offseason.

Boston has earned reps with the first-team offense , and Concepcion made a strong first impression in his preseason debut, catching three passes for 27 yards, returning a punt for 31 yards and scoring on a 14-yard run.
While Boston lines up on the perimeter in the passing game, the Browns can use Concepcion in a variety of ways on offense and special teams.

Entering his fourth season, Cedric Tillman is expendable in Cleveland.

The Browns have a lead veteran receiver and high-upside young talent behind him on the depth chart, which leaves little room for Tillman to contribute on a week-to-week basis. While he's shown flashes here and there, the 26-year-old has missed 13 games because of injuries.

Perhaps former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski will make a call to reunite with Tillman in Atlanta. Underwhelming 2022 first-rounder Jahan Dotson is trying to lock down the Falcons' No. 2 receiver spot.

articles.title: Latest 2026 NFL Free Agents Rumors, Predictions for Adoree' Jackson, Taylor Decker, More
articles.summary: While August always brings training camps and the NFL preseason, it usually brings an active final wave of free agency, too. Teams regularly scramble to address needs ahead of Week 1, as the top remaining free agents have had all summer to narrow their options.
articles.body:
While August always brings training camps and the NFL preseason, it usually brings an active final wave of free agency, too. Teams regularly scramble to address needs ahead of Week 1, as the top remaining free agents have had all summer to narrow their options.

Things have certainly been active this August, as the list of notable names who have been signed includes Jadevon Clowney, Stefon Diggs, Von Miller, Za'Darius Smith, and Keenan Allen.

While there has been a recent flurry of free-agent activity, the player pool hasn't dried up just yet. Here, we'll examine some of the biggest remaining names and latest rumors before making a few predictions.

Cowboys Looking for CB Depth, Could Eye Adoree' Jackson

The Dallas Cowboys have made a few splashes this offseason, and they made another when they signed Miller to bolster their pass rush. It appears, though, that Dallas isn't done improving its defense.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Cowboys are searching for additional cornerback depth and could target a veteran with coaching ties.

"One name to watch is Adoree Jackson, who was with DC Christian Parker in Philadelphia. Jackson has interest from a few teams, though," Fowler posted on X .

The Cowboys are circling back to a defender they targeted in the spring. NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that Jackson was visiting Dallas in May. The 30-year-old spent last season with the rival Philadelphia Eagles after spending the previous four with the New York Giants.

Dallas is likely to continue weighing options, and Jackson reportedly has interest from multiple teams. However, the prediction here is that Jackson opts for familiarity and stays in the NFC East.

Prediction: Dallas signs Jackson to a one-year deal.

Seahawks Sign Trevon Diggs, Expected to Add Terrion Arnold

Dallas' search for cornerback depth won't include one former starter.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Seattle Seahawks have agreed to a one-year deal with former Pro Bowler Trevon Diggs. The 27-year-old hasn't been the same standout defender since suffering a torn ACL in 2023. The Cowboys released him partway through last season, and he briefly joined the Green Bay Packers at the end of the year.

It's worth noting that Seattle may only view Diggs as a placeholder or insurance policy. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo , the Seahawks plan to sign former Detroit Lions starter Terrion Arnold, though it could take "a while."

Arnold faces eight felony charges related to a February kidnapping and robbery in Tampa, Florida. According to Rapoport and Garafolo, he'll be placed on the NFL commissioner's exempt list while the league looks into his case. With Diggs in the fold, Seattle should be in no rush to sign Arnold.

Prediction: Arnold remains unsigned through August 30 roster cuts.

Taylor Decker Remains Unsigned Months After Being Granted His Release

Arnold isn't the only noteworthy player who has been released by the Lions this offseason. Longtime starting left tackle Taylor Decker requested his release and was granted it in early March.

More than five months later, Decker remains unsigned.

Decker, who was graded 41st overall among offensive tackles by Pro Football Focus last season, is arguably the top lineman still available. After getting out of Detroit, he's likely looking for a more intriguing opportunity. Theoretically, he could find it with the Washington Commanders, who have lost Laremy Tunsil to a torn triceps.

According to Fowler , though, Washington plans to rely on its internal depth to navigate Tunsil's absence.

Could the Commanders' plan change after evaluating their depth in the preseason? Absolutely, and other opportunities could arise for Decker as other teams evaluate what they have up front. Don't be surprised if Decker continues waiting for his perfect fit.

Prediction: Decker remains unsigned until after August 30 roster cuts.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Saints Consider Chase Claypool, Josh Reynolds

Injuries are an unfortunate part of the NFL summer. Like the Commanders, the New Orleans Saints are dealing with one. Rookie first-round pick Jordyn Tyson is battling a right hamstring injury that could cause him to miss up to two months, according to Rapoport and Garafolo .

According to Schefter, New Orleans has kicked the tires on Chase Claypool and Hosh Reynolds as potential placeholders:

Claypool had a couple of promising seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers early in his career but hasn't appeared in a regular-season game since 2023. He attempted a comeback earlier this offseason as a tryout player at Green Bay Packers rookie minicamp.

Reynolds appeared in five games last season with the New York Jets. While neither receiver is likely to make a significant impact for the Saints, Reynolds is probably the more game-ready option.

Prediction: The Saints sign Reynolds, potentially moving him to the practice squad after August 30.

articles.title: Trey McBride, Brian Burns Named to NFL Top 100, Check Out the Updated 2026 Rankings
articles.summary: New York Giants linebacker Brian Burns clearly impressed his peers after totaling a career-high 16.5 sacks last year.
articles.body:
New York Giants linebacker Brian Burns clearly impressed his peers after totaling a career-high 16.5 sacks last year.

Burns came in at 14th in the NFL Top 100 ahead of the 2026 season after missing the cut altogether in 2025. He had previously never ranked higher than 54th.

Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride enjoyed a major bump as well, climbing from 65th to 13th.

Here's how the list looks as it inches toward its conclusion.

100. New Orleans Saints DE Cameron Jordan

99. Indianapolis Colts OG Quenton Nelson

96. New Orleans Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr.

93. Cleveland Browns LB Carson Schwesinger

87. Carolina Panthers WR Tetairoa McMillan

86. Los Angeles Chargers LB Tuli Tuipulotu

77. Tampa Bay Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield

62. Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence

52. Tampa Bay Buccaneers OT Tristan Wirfs

50. Los Angeles Chargers S Derwin James Jr.

48. Jacksonville Jaguars DE Josh Hines-Allen

47. Philadelphia Eagles CB Quinyon Mitchell

46. San Francisco 49ers TE George Kittle

40. San Francisco 49ers OT Trent Williams

39. Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert

38. Philadelphia Eagles CB Cooper DeJean

34. Philadelphia Eagles RB Saquon Barkley

28. New England Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez

25. Houston Texans CB Derek Stingley Jr.

19. Minnesota Vikings WR Justin Jefferson

18. Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes

17. Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor

New York paid a steep price to acquire Burns in 2024. The trade itself wasn't that expensive as the Giants sent second- and fifth-round draft picks to the Carolina Panthers. Far bigger was the five-year, $141 million contract he received.

Burns proceeded to register 8.5 sacks as the team went 3-14.

The Giants didn't improve much collectively last season, but the veteran edge-rusher at least justified his substantial salary.

"He was different than in years past," one anonymous coordinator told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . "He was more of a force consistently, more of a pain in the ass to play against."

New York made an aggressive play when it hired John Harbaugh and is prepared to pay him a reported $20 million annually. The front office and coaching staff may nonetheless need more than one offseason to build the franchise into a contender.

Should Burns once again play at an elite level, it might fail to move the needle in terms of the Giants' wider record.

The same goes for McBride after the Cardinals hit the reset button and hired Mike LaFleur. They were 31st in Bleacher Report's most recent power rankings before the start of training camp.

That shouldn't preclude McBride from having another 1,000-yard season. He's likely to remain a top option through the air for Jacoby Brissett, who has a low ceiling but a high floor for a starter.

The two-time Pro Bowler led the team with 169 targets. Michael Wilson was next with 126 and Marvin Harrison Jr. was a distant third at 73.

Harrison could finally assert himself as a No. 1 receiver in the NFL, and that would impact McBride's production if it happens.

But McBride showed his 2024 breakout was no fluke. As long as he stays healthy, he'll be one of the NFL's best at his position.

articles.title: Falcons Reportedly Sell Minority Stake at $10.6B Valuation Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: <p>Private equity firm Arctos is purchasing a 10 percent stake in the Atlanta Falcons, according to CNBC's <a href="https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/20/arctos-agrees-to-buy-10percent-of-atlanta-falcons-at-10point6-billion-valuation-sources.html?__source=sharebar%7Ctwitter&par=sharebar" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Michael Ozanian and Jessica Golden</a>.</p>
articles.body:
Private equity firm Arctos is purchasing a 10 percent stake in the Atlanta Falcons, according to CNBC's Michael Ozanian and Jessica Golden .

The deal values the NFL franchise at $10.6 billion. By comparison, the Seattle Seahawks are slated to change hands in a sale worth a league-record $9.6 billion.

The NFL amended its ownership rules in 2024 to allow for private equity firms to purchase minority stakes. The 10 percent sought by Arctos is the maximum share permitted.

One firm is also allowed to buy into multiple teams. Ozanian and Golden noted Arctos has already invested in the Los Angeles Chargers, Buffalo Bills and Cleveland Browns.

In the case of the Falcons, it's unclear whether majority owner Arthur Blank is cashing in on some of his shares or if Arctos worked with Atlanta's limited partners.

The Falcons having a valuation of more than $10 billion is another sign of the NFL's robust financial health. CNBC's Alex Sherman explained in 2024 how that prompted the league's owners to open the door for private equity.

The already small pool of candidates that can purchase a controlling interest in an NFL team is only getting smaller. Selling off a 10 percent stake is a way to attain some cold hard cash without divesting entirely.

Bringing Arctos into the fold probably won't impact how the Falcons operate day-to-day.

articles.title: A.J. Brown, Jalen Hurts Reunite for 1st Time Since Trade in Video from Eagles-Patriots Practice
articles.summary: One day after A.J. Brown made headlines for saying he hadn't spoken to Jalen Hurts since being traded by the Philadelphia Eagles to the New England Patriots, the two finally reconnected.
articles.body:
One day after A.J. Brown made headlines for saying he hadn't spoken to Jalen Hurts since being traded by the Philadelphia Eagles to the New England Patriots, the two finally reconnected.

After Thursday's joint practice between the Eagles and Patriots, Brown and Hurts were seen chatting with each other.

Brown did make a point yesterday after saying he and Hurts had not spoken since the July 1 trade that he wanted to "keep everything positive" and "none of that stuff even matters" anymore.

Much has been made about the dynamic between Hurts and Brown over the past 12 months. Brown offered this assessment of the relationship when asked about it earlier this summer during an interview with NBC Sports' Maria Taylor.

"Not as close as we once were," Brown said . "I believe that's fine. There's no bad blood. There's actually still a lot of love. I love him to death. I ⁠want him to succeed and accomplish all the things that he wants to accomplish."

ESPN's Tim McManus reported in May that part of Brown's frustration with the Eagles offense as a whole was "directed" at Hurts because of a "perceived reluctance to target Brown on tight-window throws in zone coverage."

Even though Brown did surpass the 1,000-yard mark in each of his four seasons with Philadelphia, there was a notable drop in his production in 2025 compared to the previous three years.

Brown's 1,003 yards marked his second-lowest output since entering the NFL, ahead of his 869 yards 2021 when he only played 13 games for the Tennessee Titans.

He also set career-lows in yards per reception (12.9) and success rate (50.4).

Despite the unceremonious end of his time with the Eagles, Brown and Hurts both had tremendous success together. They helped the team make the playoffs in each of their four years as teammates, reached the Super Bowl twice and won the Lombardi Trophy during the 2024 season.

Brown and the Patriots will take on Hurts and the Eagles in a preseason game on Saturday at Gillette Stadium.

ESPN's Tim McManus reported in May that part of Brown's frustration with the Eagles offense as a whole was "directed" at Hurts because of a "perceived reluctance to target Brown on tight-window throws in zone coverage."
Even though Brown did surpass the 1,000-yard mark in each of his four seasons with Philadelphia, there was a notable drop in his production in 2025 compared to the previous three years.
Brown's 1,003 yards marked his second-lowest output since entering the NFL, ahead of his 869 yards 2021 when he only played 13 games for the Tennessee Titans.
He also set career-lows in yards per reception (12.9) and success rate (50.4).

Despite the unceremonious end of his time with the Eagles, Brown and Hurts both had tremendous success together. They helped the team make the playoffs in each of their four years as teammates, reached the Super Bowl twice and won the Lombardi Trophy during the 2024 season.
Brown and the Patriots will take on Hurts and the Eagles in a preseason game on Saturday at Gillette Stadium.

articles.title: Vita Vea Says Bucs Trade Was 'Never the End Goal' After New Contract Extension
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea revealed that a trade was "never the end goal for me" and he "always wanted to be here" after signing a new contract extension on Thursday, according to ESPN's Jenna Laine.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea revealed that a trade was "never the end goal for me" and he "always wanted to be here" after signing a new contract extension on Thursday, according to ESPN's Jenna Laine .

"Yeah, it's just all part of the business," Vea said, per Laine. "I got drafted here. I made it my home. I made Tampa my home. I love it here. The guys on the team are like brothers to me. We look at each other as family. So I didn't want to leave that behind and switch teams and get traded."

The two-time Pro Bowler requested a trade from Tampa Bay on July 27 following multiple failed attempts at finalizing a contract extension.

Vea ultimately agreed to a new one-year, $30 million contract to stay with the team that he's spent all eight seasons of his career with.

"It's just one of those things," Vea said, via Laine. "They took a chance on me in the draft, and I've been here ever since. And I fell in love with Tampa. I fell in love with my teammates. I love the organization. Everybody who works here. I walk around every day with a smile on my face."

The extension contains $6 million in new money for Vea's 2026 campaign and keeps him under contract for two more seasons.

"They say home is where the heart is. I feel like my heart is in Tampa," he said. "I always wanted to be a Buc, and I wanted to be a Buc for life."

Vea's long-term future in Tampa Bay was murky following the trade request. It's worth noting that he was also holding in during training camp, being present at practice despite not participating in any drills while he awaited a new deal.

Still, Buccaneers general manager Jason Licht was adamant about not trading Vea while both sides worked on an extension.

"I have no plans on trading Vita," Licht said on Aug. 6, per Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times .

Tampa Bay initially selected Vea with the No. 12 overall pick in the 2018 NFL draft, as he quickly blossomed into a key starter on their defense.

He's helped the Buccaneers make five playoff appearances throughout his tenure with the team, including a 2020 season that ended with a Super Bowl LV victory.

In 17 appearances last year, Vea racked up 34 tackles, 13 quarterback hits, seven tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks. He also amassed 51 pressures, according to Pro Football Focus .

As the Buccaneers look to capture a sixth consecutive NFC South title in 2026, Vea won't be going anywhere.

articles.title: Giants' Jameis Winston Punched by Dolphins Player on Video During Fight-Filled Joint Practice
articles.summary: Things got chippy between the New York Giants and Miami Dolphins during a joint practice on Thursday.
articles.body:
Things got chippy between the New York Giants and Miami Dolphins during a joint practice on Thursday.

A massive brawl broke out during the practice, and Giants quarterback Jameis Winston took a punch from a Dolphins player.

Dolphins offensive tackle Austin Jackson and Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor also had to be pulled off the field after the fight, according to ESPN's Jordan Raanan and Marcel Louis-Jacques .

Jackson threw a punch at Giants rookie linebacker Arvell Reese. He was also pushed to the ground by linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux after punching Reese.

After getting involved in the skirmish, Winston also had to be removed for a handful of plays.

The fights occurred despite a warning from Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley, who said players who threw a punch would be kicked out and that he would be "very, very disappointed" to have to remove a player from practice.

"In this sort of an environment, you have these rules of engagement that aren't really rules of the game, and then somebody else goes over the line or they do go over the line and somebody needs to protect somebody and that's where it goes. And I think as long as it doesn't get out of control, where it gets a violent-type situation, it's fine, you know?" Giants coach John Harbaugh said. "And we decided that anybody that threw a punch in those scrimmages would be treated like the game. That's why Jermaine didn't practice toward the end. He didn't really throw a hard punch, but it was to the facemask. And that'll get you in the game. That's a 15-yarder at least."

That kind of physicality isn't all that surprising at this point during training camp. Players are eager to get back on the field against real competition rather than their own teammates, so they're coming into these joint practices fired up.

The Giants and Dolphins will play a preseason game on Saturday, where Harbaugh and Hafley will look to get better behavior from their players.

articles.title: Top NFL Bargain Free Agents Remaining After Keenan Allen, Trevon Diggs, Taylor Rapp Deals
articles.summary: NFL training camps are reaching their conclusion, and the preseason is in full swing. This means, of course, that teams are discovering new holes to fill and turning back to the free-agent market to fill them.
articles.body:
NFL training camps are reaching their conclusion, and the preseason is in full swing. This means, of course, that teams are discovering new holes to fill and turning back to the free-agent market to fill them.

Recent signings featured some big names like Jadeveon Clowney, Stefon Diggs, and Von Miller. However, it has also included potential bargain signings like those of wide receiver Keenan Allen, cornerback Trevon Diggs and safety Taylor Rapp.

The good news for teams still looking to address needs is that several more potential bargains remain unsigned and available.

Here, you'll find the top bargain free agents left on the market, why they could be intriguing options, and possible landing spots based on team needs, past performance, player potential, and recent buzz.

Mekhi Becton was a 2020 first-round pick out of Louisville. However, injuries and underwhelming play prevented him from ever living up to his draft status during his time with the New York Jets.

Becton was again hampered by poor performances and injuries in the 2025 season.

The 27-year-old appeared in 17 games for the Los Angeles Chargers but battled numerous ailments and was graded 79th overall among guards by Pro Football Focus .

Becton stayed mostly healthy in 2024 and performed at an extremely high level with the Philadelphia Eagles. There's no guarantee he can return to that form, but a team that signs him to an incentive-laden "prove-it" deal could reap significant rewards if he does.

Becton would make the most sense for a potential contender that is willing to gamble on his upside, as Philadelphia did in 2024. The Detroit Lions, who have a competition brewing at left guard, and the Seattle Seahawks would be two logical suitors.

The Seahawks would likely view Becton as depth, but they are clearly open to reclamation projects, as evidenced by their recent signing of Trevon Diggs.

Logical Landing Spots: Detroit Lions, Seattle Seahawks

After the Lions failed to work out a contract adjustment with Taylor Decker, the longtime starting left tackle was granted his release from the team. The soon-to-be 33-year-old has been available ever since.

While Decker's experience should be valued—he's started all 140 games in which he has appeared—his age and recent performance should leave him open to a modest, incentive-laden deal. He was graded 41st among offensive tackles by Pro Football Focus last season.

Decker would be a sensible option for the Washington Commanders, who lost left tackle Laremy Tunsil to a torn triceps—though Washington plans to replace Tunsil with an in-house option, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

The Chicago Bears would also be a solid landing spot for Decker, and not just because of his connection to Ben Johnson. The Bears have late-2025 starter Ozzy Trapilo coming off a torn patellar tendon and no clear leader in their camp competition at left tackle.

"It's been a little bit of a revolving door," Johnson said, per The Athletic's Dan Wiederer .

Logical Landing Spots: Chicago Bears, Washington Commanders

We've seen a run on pass-rushers in August, with Clowney joining the Houston Texans, Miller joining the Dallas Cowboys, and Za'Darius Smith landing with the Atlanta Falcons.

Leonard Floyd, who started 15 games for Atlanta last season, could be the next pass-rushing domino to fall. While he recorded just 3.5 sacks in 2025, he added five tackles for loss, 11 quarterback hits, and 19 QB pressures .

Pass-rushers generally draw a premium in free agency, but with Clowney, Miller and Smith off the market, Floyd may be available on a value contract.

Even after adding Smith, the Falcons should have some interest in bringing back Floyd. Jalon Walker is out for the year with a torn ACL. Fellow 2025 first-round pick James Pearce Jr. has been suspended for the first eight games of the 2026 season under the NFL's personal-conduct policy.

The Cleveland Browns should also take a look at Floyd. They thought they had landed Smith but lost him at the last minute to former head coach Kevin Stefanski and the Falcons.

Browns edge-defender Alex Wright also exited Thursday's practice on a cart with a reported leg injury .

Logical Landing Spots: Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Cornerback Adoree' Jackson was a bargain contributor for the Eagles last season. He played on a low-risk one-year, $1.8 million contract but ended up making 10 starts for the Philly defense. He allowed an opposing passer rating of only 80.2 in coverage and chipped in with three punt returns on special teams.

If Jackson is willing to sign another budget contract, he'll provide immense value again in 2026. According to Fowler , Jackson has already drawn interest from "a few teams" and could be an option for the rival Cowboys.

"The Cowboys have explored cornerback help via free agency," Fowler posted on X.

As Fowler pointed out, Dallas' new defensive coordinator, Christian Parker, coached Jackson as the Eagles' defensive backs coach in 2025.

Jackson would also be a logical target for the Washington Commanders, who ranked 31st in net yards per pass attempt and 32nd in total yards allowed last season. Washington added Amik Robertson, Fabian Moreau, and Rasul Douglas to its cornerback room in free agency but could afford to take a flier on its former divisional foe.

Logical Landing Spots: Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders

The Indianapolis Colts and Kenny Moore II agreed to mutually work on a trade early in the offseason. After weeks of failing to find a trade partner, the Colts opted to release the cornerback instead.

Given the lack of trade interest, Moore can only expect modest offers at this point. A team that signs him to a team-friendly contract, however, could get a big bargain. Moore will turn 31 later this month and made just seven starts last season, but he also allowed an opposing passer rating of just 87.8 in coverage in 2025.

He would be a sensible target for Dallas, given its interest in adding cornerback depth. He'd also be a good fit as a depth piece with the San Francisco 49ers.

New 49ers defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus previously coached Moore as the Colts' defensive coordinator.

Logical Landing Spots: Dallas Cowboys, San Francisco 49ers

Offensive tackle Cam Robinson signed a one-year, $12 million deal with the Texans last offseason. However, he was traded to Cleveland in-season and didn't perform particularly well with either franchise.

Pro Football Focus graded Robinson 83rd overall among offensive tackles in 2025.

Due to his performance last season, Robinson can likely be had at a fraction of his 2025 salary. He may also be more valuable as a depth piece than an expected starter.

That said, Robinson does have 114 starts on his resume and is still only 30 years old. He'd be a terrific insurance option for a playoff hopeful with questionable depth at left tackle.

The Commanders may believe that Brandon Coleman can replace Tunsil, but adding Robinson couldn't hurt. Given the importance of protecting Joe Burrow, the Cincinnati Bengals should also consider Robinson as a Plan B behind Orlando Brown Jr.

Logical Landing Spots: Cincinnati Bengals, Washington Commanders

Tight end Jonnu Smith had a Pro Bowl campaign with the Miami Dolphins in 2024 but was far less effective with the Pittsburgh Steelers this past season. He caught just 32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns while sharing reps with Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth.

The Steelers released Smith after one year.

While the 31-year-old is unlikely to replicate his 2024 production (884 yards, 8 TDs), he'd be a terrific insurance policy for a pass-heavy team with injury concerns at the tight end position.

The 49ers could partner Smith with Jake Tonges as George Kittle continues to work his way back from a torn Achilles. The Lions could use a pass-catching move tight end behind Sam LaPorta, who is dealing with a hip injury.

According to ESPN's Eric Woodyard , LaPorta's status for Week 1 is unclear.

Logical Landing Spots: Detroit Lions, San Francisco 49ers

Haason Reddick is another edge-defender who should garner interest with Clowney, Smith and Miller off the board—Joey Bosa is also unsigned but appears to be leaning toward retirement.

"It is more likely than not that Joey Bosa has played his last NFL down," ESPN's Adam Schefter said on his podcast in July (h/t ProFootballTalk's Josh Alper ).

Reddick had just 2.5 sacks with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last season and had just one sack in 10 games with the Jets the previous season. After two disappointing years, he's probably looking at a bargain contract in late free agency. However, he logged 11 sacks with the Eagles in 2023.

A contract dispute led the Eagles to trade Reddick to the Jets in 2024. A reunion would make sense, as Jonathan Greenard is now dealing with a pectoral injury and could miss the start of the regular season.

Reddick could also be an option for the Browns, who were " hopeful " about signing Clowney before losing both him and Smith to other teams in free agency.

Logical Landing Spots: Cleveland Browns, Philadelphia Eagles

Linebacker Bobby Wagner turned 36 in June, but if he wants to start this season, he should find multiple opportunities. The reigning Walter Payton Man of the Year started all 17 games for the Commanders last season and finished with 162 tackles, 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss, and two interceptions.

Even if Wagner matches last year's $9 million salary, he'll be a relative bargain if he can produce similar numbers.

Landing with a Super Bowl contender would make the most sense at this stage in Wagner's career. The Denver Broncos are expected to be that, and they could certainly use an off-ball linebacker.

Justin Strnad is a solid starter, but Alex Singleton has been a liability against the pass, and Denver lacks depth behind those two at inside linebacker.

The Cowboys may not be viewed as title contenders, but they have an improved defense, could use help at the second level, and have a Wagner fan in head coach Brian Schottenheimer—who spent time with the future Hall of Famer in Seattle.

"You're looking at one of the biggest Bobby Wagner fans in the world," Schottenheimer told Kay Adams of Up & Adams in March. "...I love that guy."

Logical Landing Spots: Dallas Cowboys, Denver Broncos

Guard Kevin Zeitler has largely been a reliable starter throughout his 14-year career. He was arguably the Tennessee Titans' most dependable lineman last season, earning a 13th-place overall grade among guards from Pro Football Focus .

Zeitler is still a starting-caliber lineman who can help either a contender or a rebuilding team. At 36 years old, though, he isn't going to be a long-term option and should be available on a modest one-year deal.

The Chargers could consider bringing in Zeitler to help bolster the depth of an offensive interior that was decimated by injuries in 2025 and recently lost center Tyler Biadasz to an ACL injury .

Zeitler would also make sense as insurance for New York Giants rookie guard Francis Mauigoa . He spent three seasons, including his lone Pro Bowl campaign, playing for the Baltimore Ravens and John Harbaugh, who is now New York's head coach.

Logical Landing Spots: Los Angeles Chargers, New York Giants

*Contract and cap information via Spotrac . Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference .

articles.title: Watch Fernando Mendoza Shout Out Joe Buck on Live Broadcast Video During Raiders vs. Texans
articles.summary: In addition to showing off his football talent in Thursday's preseason contest against the Houston Texans, Fernando Mendoza also brought out the "aw-shucks" part of his personality at one point.
articles.body:
In addition to showing off his football talent in Thursday's preseason contest against the Houston Texans, Fernando Mendoza also brought out the "aw-shucks" part of his personality at one point.

While being interviewed on the sidelines by ESPN's Laura Rutledge, Mendoza gave a shoutout to play-by-play commentator Joe Buck as only he can.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Most NFL players would likely think to acknowledge Troy Aikman, a Pro Football Hall of Famer and Buck's longtime broadcast partner. Mendoza opted to go for the lead man in the booth because he "needs some more love."

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Best Strategy for Each Pick in 12-Team Mock Drafts
articles.summary: The start of the 2026 NFL preseason's second week is a great reminder that the busy drafting weekend on the fantasy football calender is fast approaching.
articles.body:
The start of the 2026 NFL preseason's second week is a great reminder that the busy drafting weekend on the fantasy football calender is fast approaching.

If you haven't nailed down your draft strategy quite yet, time is absolutely of the essence.

Let's act with some urgency, then, and get right into building an early-round blueprint for each pick position in a 12-team mock draft.

The right target at the 1-1 spot will offer superstar upside with a good amount of safety. That feels like the perfect description for Bijan Robinson, who just reeled off 2,298 scrimmage yards with 11 scores and somehow still seems capable of more. With perhaps the best running back on your roster, you should value playmakers at the 2/3 turn, either doubling up on receiver or spending one pick on a star tight end (Trey McBride or Brock Bowers).

This should be a simple decision, as you can just lock in on whichever of Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs is left on the board. If it's Gibbs (as it would be here), you should plan on adding a second running back in Rounds 2 or 3 (adding a receiver with the other), just in case Detroit's collection of playmakers starts cutting into Gibbs' touchdown tally.

Ja'Marr Chase gets the slight nod over Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Puka Nacua for arguably offering the best blend of ceiling and floor. Chase is probably WR1 if Joe Burrow stays healthy all season, and he would still be an elite option even if Joe Flacco gets forced into action. Target running back in the second round, and you'll be in good shape to take the best player available in the third.

Nacua will be tempting here, but add Smith-Njigba instead. Seattle's passing volume could increase given the club's questions at running back (no Kenneth Walker III and a still-recovering Zach Charbonnet), and JSN doesn't have a ton of competition for targets. Look for any falling values with your next two picks and give serious consideration to making an elite tight end one of them.

Nacua is almost a PPR cheat code as the No. 1 target in the league's most prolific passing attack. He would be awesome to pair with the top running back on the board in Round 2, and if no one has reached at the positions, you could go tight end or even quarterback in Round 3, potentially giving you a top performer at three different positions with your first three picks.

There is arguably a tier drop here, but maybe there isn't if Jonathan Taylor just stays on the field. During the two seasons in which he made 17 appearances (2025 being one of them), he racked up 4,134 scrimmage yards and 40 touchdowns. With some injuries in his past, though, you should double-tap running back with your second pick just to solidify that strength, then aim for a receiver in Round 3.

Amon-Ra St. Brown is your first-round target, and he's a really good one—always a high-level producer, sometimes a truly awesome one. His elevated floor allows for a risk-reward wager in Round 2 (think Nico Collins, A.J. Brown or Malik Nabers). If you like the depth at running back and believe you could get a good one in Round 4, don't rule out a top-shelf quarterback in Round 3.

This might be a coin-flip call between CeeDee Lamb and Justin Jefferson, but those players don't settle the debate. Rather, the quarterbacks do, so take Lamb and bet on Dak Prescott over Kyler Murray. Running back should be your Round 2 priority (De'Von Achane, Omarion Hampton, Chase Brown), and then circle back to receiver for an upside play in Round 3 to account for Lamb's availability issues (five games missed the past two seasons) and erratic touchdown tally (nine scores over the same stretch).

Last season proved Justin Jefferson isn't immune to horrific quarterback play, but he's still a good value play here. Kyler Murray could stabilize the position, and if he does, Jefferson might be the WR1. You'll still want a second receiver among your first three picks to account for the volatility of Minnesota's passing game, but running back is probably your best Round 2 bet.

There are legitimate worries with Christian McCaffrey (a 30-year-old with a long injury history and a 413-touch workload last season), but they've been accounted for this point. Grab CMC, and you might have just taken the top performer in fantasy (if healthy, obviously) with the 10th overall pick. Add a second running back in Round 2 to safeguard against McCaffrey's risks. In Round 3, you might consider tight ends or quarterbacks if you don't love how wide receiver looks.

This feels like a sweet spot for Ashton Jeanty. He overcome a rough ecosystem to deliver 1,321 scrimmage yards and 10 scores as a rookie, and his Las Vegas Raiders have since made major investments to their quarterback room and offensive line. Take the best wide receiver on the board in Round 2, and if Josh Allen makes it to you in Round 3, take him. You'll have legitimate stars at the three most important positions.

With back-to-back picks to open things up, try a double-tap at running back with James Cook III and De'Von Achane. Both were top-7 running backs last season, but they do have some questions (possible touchdown regression for Cook, Miami's offensive infrastructure for Achane). You can mitigate your risks by taking both. A double-tap at receiver at the 3/4 turn is probably your best option, but if Allen slips, he'd be a fun addition.

articles.title: Texans Sign 2 WRs as NFL Trade Rumors Link Patriots' Boutte, Ravens' Bateman After Higgins Injury
articles.summary: The Houston Texans have signed both Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones after hosting the wide receivers for workouts on Friday, per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans have signed both Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones after hosting the wide receivers for workouts on Friday, per NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

The news comes after KPRC 2's Aaron Wilson reported that Houston made some "exploratory trade calls" after learning about wide receiver Jayden Higgins' season-ending injury .

The New England Patriots' Kayshon Boutte and Baltimore Ravens' Rashod Bateman were labeled "potential targets" for the Texans prior to Shepard and Jones' contracts, according to Wilson.

Free agent wideout Josh Reynolds was also "on the team's radar," per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Higgins suffered a torn ACL during a joint practice against the Las Vegas Raiders earlier this week, ESPN and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Wednesday.

Shepard, who spent the first eight years of his career with the New York Giants, spent the last two seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In 2025, he caught 39 passes for 371 yards and one touchdown in 13 games.

Jones, meanwhile, has played for four different teams throughout his nine-year career--the Buffalo Bills, Las Vegas Raiders, Jacksonville Jaguars and Arizona Cardinals. He spent the last two seasons in Arizona.

In 2025, Jones caught 12 passes for 183 yards in eight games. His best season came in 2022 with Jacksonville, where he caught 82 passes for 823 yards and five scores.

Boutte has been floated as a potential trade candidate since the Patriots acquired A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs this offseason.

Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer reported in May he felt Boutte could be acquired at the time "for a fifth- or sixth-round draft pick."

Bateman has also been linked to trade possibilities in the past as the Ravens continue turning to Zay Flowers as the team's top wide receiver.

ESPN's Rich Cimini reported in May the New York Jets were considering Bateman alongside three other receivers as trade targets.

However, it's reasonable to think that the Texans are now out on both receivers.

Higgins suffered his season-ending injury after a fall during 11-on-11 drills in the red zone, per ESPN's DJ Bien-Aime .

He was primed to take on a bigger role during his sophomore NFL season after posting 41 catches for 525 receiving yards and six touchdowns in 17 games and 10 starts of the 2025 campaign.

Houston's ability to replace him will be tested by other injuries to the team's wide receiver room. Tank Dell is still working his way back from the knee injury that sidelined him for the entirety of the 2025 season, while Jaylin Noel has been dealing with right pinkie and hamstring injuries .

The Texans have just over a week before the NFL requires teams cut their rosters down to 53 players on Sunday, Aug. 30.

articles.title: Live NFL Preseason Week 2 Fantasy Football Takeaways and Advice from Friday's Games
articles.summary: The second week of the NFL preseason is well underway. It's less than three weeks until the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots in a rematch of Super Bowl LX that marks the official beginning of the 2026 NFL season—and with it, another season of fantasy football.
articles.body:
The preseason is a time of great hope. And great hype.

Broncos running back Jonah Coleman is the source of both right now. Not that long ago, Coleman was just a Day 3 rookie joining a crowded Broncos backfield. But after less than 10 preseason carries, some are already anointing the 5'8", 220-pounder the future in the Denver backfield .

The Broncos have seen something they like—after one series and three carries against the Green Bay Packers, Coleman got the bubble-wrap treatment. And with an ADP in the 12th round, whether the future is now or not doesn't really matter. There's also JK Dobbins' durability issues to consider.

But unless Dobbins (or RJ Harvey) gets hurt, Coleman isn't going to see more than a handful of touches per game. And for all the hoopla, we're talking about a guy with seven carries for 33 yards against backups.

articles.title: Jets Record 2 INTs vs. Steelers After Making NFL History with Zero Picks During 2025-26 Season
articles.summary: The New York Jets defense had more success picking off passes in one preseason game than they did all of last season.
articles.body:
The New York Jets defense had more success picking off passes in one preseason game than they did all of last season.

The Jets picked off the Pittsburgh Steelers twice during Friday night's preseason action after becoming the first team since at least 1933 to go a full season without an interception.

The picks were thrown by Steelers quarterback Will Howard on back-to-back drives during the second quarter.

The first interception came at the Jets' 14-yard line, when Howard tried to find Roman Wilson on a short pass that was picked off by the Jets' Andre Cisco.

On the following drive at the Jets' 37-yard line, Howard again tried to find Wilson for a short pass and was picked off by Samuel Womack.

It's been almost exactly a year since the Jets last recorded an interception when Malachi Moore picked off an overthrown pass from Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Kyle McCord on Aug. 22, 2025.

Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright said earlier this offseason he didn't think the team's lack of interceptions last season had been brought up in meetings, per NyJets.com's Jack Bell .

"I think 2025 was 2025 and I think we're trying to turn over a new leaf, so we haven't spoken about it at all," Wright said, per Bell.

The Jets will now hope to build on Friday's defensive performance when opening the regular season Sept. 13 against the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: Eagles' 'Bumpy Road' Explained in New NFL Rumors and Latest Fantasy Outlook on Jalen Hurts, Saquon
articles.summary: Expectations are high for Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, though there have been some growing pains during training camp.
articles.body:
Expectations are high for Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, though there have been some growing pains during training camp.

"They're really happy with how open he's been to the changes, taking under-center work, play action, ball fakes, all that stuff," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler said on Saturday's SportsCenter regarding Hurts. "He's really taken to the footwork part of it; got to work early in the offseason. He and Sean Mannion have hit it off in that way. Now, they had a joint practice with the Patriots for two days. The sentiment was it was a little up and down; first day was a little bit rough. That was to be expected because a lot of the receivers had been out. De'Vonta Smith had a hamstring issue, missed multiple weeks. First-round pick Makai Lemon, hamstring, missed multiple weeks. They're finally getting healthy and back into the swing. Hurts doesn't really play in preseason games, so it's expected to be a bit of a bumpy road as they get the offense in full swing. They're hoping by Week 1 they're full strength and then the running game is going to be big. The sentiment there is that with Saquon Barkley getting back to those 20-, 30-yard runs, that will set the stage for Hurts to have a big year."

The Eagles had their share of struggles on offense last season, as the play-calling of offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo and head coach Nick Sirianni often became predictable and stale.

But Hurts also had an up-and-down season, throwing for 3,224 yards, 25 touchdowns and six interceptions while completing 64.8 percent of his passes, taking 32 sacks and rushing for 421 yards and eight touchdowns. The numbers were fine, but Hurts and the Eagles left a lot of meat on the bone in the passing game.

In addition, a once-dominant offensive line battled through a number of injuries and was less ineffective than seasons past. Barkley was pressing, often finding himself trying to make a defender miss before even reaching the line of scrimmage. Wideout A.J. Brown spent much of the season unhappy with the state of the passing game and offense, and wasn't particularly shy in letting those feelings be known publicly.

The result was an offense that ranked 24th in total yards (311.2 YPG), 23rd in passing (194.3 YPG) and 19th in scoring (22.3 PPG). The Eagles still made the playoffs but lost to the San Francisco 49ers in the Wild Card Round.

Major changes followed, with Mannion replacing Patullo. The hope is that his scheme—which will rely more on pre-snap motion, under-center plays and working the middle of the field in the passing game—will revitalize both Hurts and the rest of the offense. So far, the transition has shown real promise.

Hurts is always a viable option in fantasy, given his rushing touchdowns, but a more productive year through the air would give him the potential to be a top-three option at the position. That's the best-case scenario, however, especially with Hurts adjusting to life without Brown. But realistically, Hurts is still a safe starter on a weekly basis.

As for Barkley, a major bounceback season could be brewing, especially if the offensive line is healthy. Don't expect another 2,000-yard season on the ground, but it wouldn't be shocking if he's a top-five running back this season.

articles.title: Bears Donate $200K to Support Illinois, Indiana Communities Affected by Severe Storms
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears announced Saturday that they are donating $200,000 to aid in recovery from severe storms and flooding that impacted the southern suburbs of Chicago and Northwest Indiana.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears announced Saturday that they are donating $200,000 to aid in recovery from severe storms and flooding that impacted the southern suburbs of Chicago and Northwest Indiana.

Donations will be split evenly with $100,000 going to Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Chicago and $100,000 being provided to Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Gary.

The Bears noted that both organizations are "helping address immediate and ongoing needs in affected communities, including food, clothing, housing assistance and other recovery resources where many families remain without power, displaced from their homes and face a long rebuilding process."

According to ABC7 in Chicago, at least seven storm-related deaths were reported, and nearly 150,000 customers were still without power in Northwest Indiana as of last Sunday.

articles.title: Anthony Richardson, Top Players' Final Box Score Stats and Highlights from Falcons vs. Colts
articles.summary: Anthony Richardson didn't do himself any favors in his battle for the Indianapolis Colts' backup quarterback job during the team's 34-6 preseason loss to the Atlanta Falcons at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Saturday.
articles.body:
Anthony Richardson didn't do himself any favors in his battle for the Indianapolis Colts' backup quarterback job during the team's 34-6 preseason loss to the Atlanta Falcons at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Saturday.

Despite entering the game as 3.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel , the Colts faltered out of the gate and were outscored 24-6 in the first half.

Here is a look at the stat lines for Richardson and other notable contributors from the second game of the preseason for both Indianapolis and Atlanta:

With starting quarterback Daniel Jones sitting, Colts head coach Shane Steichen decided to give Riley Leonard and Richardson one half each in order to stake their claim to the QB2 spot.

After getting the start, Leonard struggled to get much going on offense during the first half, going just 7-of-14 for 62 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. He then gave way to Richardson, who played the entire second half.

The offense didn't look any better with Richardson at the helm, as the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft went just 3-of-9 for 24 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions through the air, while also rushing for 15 yards on three carries.

Neither Tua Tagovailoa nor Michael Penix Jr. saw action at quarterback for the Falcons, but their offense ran far more smoothly than Indy's nonetheless.

Even with star skill-position players in running back Bijan Robinson, wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts all sitting, both Cooper Rush and Jack Strand impressed under center for Atlanta.

Rush got the start and played most of the first half, going 10-of-11 for 86 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions.

Strand took over late in the first half and played the entire second half, going 12-of-17 for 212 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions. He also rushed for 22 yards and a score on nine totes.

An undrafted rookie out of Division II Minnesota State-Moorhead, Strand has been a revelation for the Falcons so far this preseason.

After Tagovailoa and Rush both played poorly in the Falcons' 27-7 loss to the Denver Broncos in their preseason opener, Strand was responsible for Atlanta's only points, as he rushed for a one-yard touchdown.

Despite entering the game as 3.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel , the Colts faltered out of the gate and were outscored 24-6 in the first half.
Here is a look at the stat lines for Richardson and other notable contributors from the second game of the preseason for both Indianapolis and Atlanta:

articles.title: Michael Penix Jr. Takes Big Step in Knee Injury Rehab amid Falcons QB1 Battle with Tua
articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons quarterback and potential starter Michael Penix Jr. has taken a step forward in his recovery from knee surgery.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback and potential starter Michael Penix Jr. has taken a step forward in his recovery from knee surgery.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said Saturday Penix has been cleared for 11-on-11 practice.

When asked how the Falcons planned to ramp Penix up to game speed, Stefanski said, "He'll practice Monday in team periods."

Penix has previously been limited to quarterback drills and seven-on-seven practice while rehabbing from the torn ACL he suffered last November.

Stefanski has yet to announce whether Penix or Tua Tagovailoa will be starting when the Falcons kick off the regular season Sept. 13 at the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Penix tore his left ACL while playing against the Carolina Panthers on Nov. 16 and underwent surgery later that month.

That marked the third ACL repair surgery for Penix, who recovered from two torn right ACLs while playing for Indiana.

Penix told reporters last week recovery from his latest injury was not just a physical but also a mental process of learning to trust his knee again.

"If something bad happened to you, and you remember every step that took up to that place that something bad happened to you, the next time you're going to do it, you're going to think about it again... it's like, okay, yes, I am healthy, but do I trust that?" Penix said last week.

Getting Penix back on the field for full team drills could be key to the team naming a QB1, which Stefanski declined to do when announcing Tagovailoa would start the team's preseason opener.

Tagovailoa played two drives in that preseason opener and did not see action in the Falcons' Saturday matchup as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand played against the Indianapolis Colts.

Quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt said last week he felt Penix had "done everything he could possibly do to put himself in position to compete" for the QB1 position despite missing out on full team drills.

"We'll reset and kind of take a look at it from the big picture once he's available," Van Pelt said about the quarterback competition.

Depending on how Penix's participation in practice goes this week, the Falcons could potentially have all four of their quarterbacks available when wrapping up the preseason Friday against Tagovalioa's former teammates on the Miami Dolphins.

articles.title: Everything Todd Monken Said About Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson and Browns' QB1 Battle
articles.summary: Head coach Todd Monken spoke on the quarterback play of both Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson following Saturday's 31-7 preseason loss against the Buffalo Bills, though he didn't offer a timeline for naming a starter.
articles.body:
Head coach Todd Monken spoke on the quarterback play of both Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson following Saturday's 31-7 preseason loss against the Buffalo Bills, though he didn't offer a timeline for naming a starter.

He did say, however, that he was impressed with Sanders' improvement at getting the ball out faster and overall was proud of the development the second-year quarterback made made:

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

He also said he was proud of how Watson has worked this summer and addressed the fans booing him after a rough overall performance on Saturday:

Sanders started the game and was solid if unspectacular, finishing 9-of-11 for 74 yards with a touchdown, interception and sack taken. The interception wasn't great, however, as he threw behind his receiver on a short slant and the ball deflected into the air.

Watson was awful, meanwhile, finishing 5-of-12 for 36 yards and an interception. The pick came on a rough overthrow.

At this point, the Browns don't seem to have a great option. Sanders threw 10 interceptions and took 23 sacks in eight appearances last season, and already has a pair of picks during the preseason.

Watson hasn't looked like a viable starter since his Houston days, though he did look much better in the first preseason game (11-of-15 for 126 yards).

In the long term, starting Sanders and deciding whether he could be a viable starter going forward probably makes the most sense. The Browns have a pair of first round picks in 2027 in a draft that is expected to be deeper at quarterback than 2026, giving them flexibility to move up the board if needed. That essentially means Sanders has a one-year window left to prove he could be the guy.

Monken, on the other hand, is a first-year head coach and is plenty incentivized to prove he can win in the short term. If Watson was clearly winning this quarterback battle, that would mean rolling with him to start the season. But Watson has hardly removed any doubt, leaving Monken with a very interesting decision to ponder.

articles.title: Ty Simpson, Stetson Bennett's Final Box Score Stats & Highlights from Saints vs. Rams
articles.summary: Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett led the Los Angeles Rams to a 34-0 preseason victory over the New Orleans Saints on Saturday.
articles.body:
Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett led the Los Angeles Rams to a 34-0 preseason victory over the New Orleans Saints on Saturday.

The two quarterbacks combined to throw for 254 yards in the rout at Sofi Stadium.

Bennett played all of the first half and parts of the third quarter.

He led the Rams on four scoring drives in the first half. Two of them resulted in touchdowns and the other two in field goals.

Bennett did damage with his legs around the goal line. He had touchdown runs of one and eight yards.

Simpson took over in the third quarter and led the Rams on a touchdown drive in the fourth quarter.

Simpson completed four passes on the scoring drive, including a 24-yard pass play that connected with tight end Dan Villari.

Bennett and Simpson should each receive more chances to shine in the final preseason game. The Rams take on the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday to round out their preseason slate before they head to Australia to face the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Admits He Forgot About Coin Toss as Captain for Browns-Bills, 'A Laughing Moment'
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders admitted he didn't know his appointment as game captain indicated he was meant to be involved in the coin toss ahead of Saturday's preseason matchup against the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders admitted he didn't know his appointment as game captain indicated he was meant to be involved in the coin toss ahead of Saturday's preseason matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

"Pretty good day. But I messed up before I got on the field," Sanders said during a mid-game sideline interview. "I didn't go out for the coin toss.

"I knew I was the captain, but I just thought I was like the captain of the team for the week. I didn't know I was captain of the coin toss. It was a laughing moment with Coach Monken and everybody... I'm happy I got that out of the way."

Sanders, who is competing with Deshaun Watson for the Browns' QB1 position, made his first start of the preseason Saturday against the Bills.

He went 9-for-11 with 74 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception. Coach Todd Monken said after the game he'd been impressed by Sanders' command of the huddle.

Monken, who has previously indicated he plans to name a starter early next week, said Saturday he would wait to make any further decisions until he can watch tape from the Bills game.

Sanders will hope his play outweighs his pregame gaffe if Monken ultimately names a starting quarterback ahead of the Browns' preseason finale Thursday against the New England Patriots.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Trade, Demotion to QB3 Behind Carson Wentz Floated by NFL Insider After Kyler Battle
articles.summary: One prominent NFL insider isn't so sure J.J. McCarthy has any future on the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
One prominent NFL insider isn't so sure J.J. McCarthy has any future on the Minnesota Vikings.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler suggested Sunday on SportsCenter the Vikings "field a few trade calls" for the 2024 first-round pick. Should he remain in Minnesota to start the regular season, McCarthy may not even be the backup to Kyler Murray, with Carson Wentz bumping him to third in the depth chart.

Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell named Murray the starter before the team opened the preseason, and McCarthy has done little since then to show that was the wrong decision.

The third-year signal-caller went 4-of-7 for 34 yards in a 13-10 win over the New York Giants. Then he was 5-of-10 for 81 yards as Minnesota lost 13-3 to the Baltimore Ravens on Saturday.

McCarthy completed a nice 50-yard pass to Tai Felton in the first quarter against Baltimore.

On the whole, however, it was a lackluster showing. One of his persistent issues was on display as he struggled with his touch on shorter throws.

The fact McCarthy missed his entire rookie year through injury can't be an excuse anymore. Somebody selected 10th overall should be further along in his development.

It's bad enough the Vikings brought Murray in and quickly installed him as QB1. Should McCarthy lose out on the backup gig to Wentz, there may be no coming back for him in Minneapolis. The coaching staff would be displaying little faith in his talent right now.

There's no chance Minnesota would recoup its original investment from a trade, but there's likely to be at least one team willing to give something up to see if McCarthy can thrive in a new setting.

articles.title: Christian Gonzalez Contract Talks Addressed by Patriots EVP Following NFL Rumors over Kraft's Remark
articles.summary: New England Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf provided an update on contract talks between the team and star cornerback Christian Gonzalez on Saturday.
articles.body:
New England Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf provided an update on contract talks between the team and star cornerback Christian Gonzalez on Saturday.

During halftime of the Patriots' preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles (h/t ESPN's Mike Reiss ), Wolf addressed the situation, saying, "Each side is trying to do what's right for them. Christian is a tremendous player that we've been on record multiple times saying we want him to be here, and that hasn't changed. We're going to continue working with his representation to try to get something done."

Wolf's comments came on the heels of ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler reporting last Sunday on SportsCenter that Gonzalez was not thrilled with Patriots owner Robert Kraft publicly saying that the organization made him an offer to be the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history.

"With the Patriots and Gonzalez, not as much optimism [as the Seattle Seahawks and cornerback Devon Witherspoon], hasn't been as smooth as a negotiation," Fowler said. "Robert Kraft, the owner, had said publicly, 'Hey, we offered him to make him the highest-paid corner in the league; he didn't take it.' I don't sense Gonzalez loved that all that much. So, there's been some back and forth. At least the Witherspoon deal creates some urgency where they can now get this done; they have a benchmark to top."

Given that Witherspoon recently signed a four-year, $132 million extension with the Seahawks that will pay him $33 million per year, Fowler speculated that negotiations between Gonzalez and the Pats should start at around $35 million per year.

Selected 17th overall in the 2023 NFL draft out of Oregon, Gonzalez has posted back-to-back strong campaigns after an injury limited him to just four games as a rookie.

In 2024, Gonzalez recorded 59 tackles, two interceptions and 11 passes defended en route to being named a Second Team All-Pro.

Gonzalez did not have a pick last season, but he did finish with 69 tackles and 10 pass breakups, resulting in his first career Pro Bowl selection.

Most notably, Gonzalez had the interception against the Denver Broncos in the AFC Championship Game that sealed the deal and punched New England's ticket to the Super Bowl.

Per Reiss, Gonzalez has not practiced since taking a hard fall in the end zone on Aug. 10, leading to speculation that his absence has been at least partially influenced by his contract situation.

Gonzalez is under team control for two more years, as the Patriots exercised the fifth-year option in his rookie contract for 2027, but it is clear that Gonzalez and his camp are pushing for a long-term deal before the start of the 2026 regular season.

articles.title: Saints Trade for 49ers RB After Alvin Kamara Injury, Full Deal Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints reportedly added some much-needed running back depth on Sunday, trading linebacker Deion Jones to the San Francisco 49ers for halfback Zamir White, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints reportedly added some much-needed running back depth on Sunday, trading linebacker Deion Jones to the San Francisco 49ers for halfback Zamir White, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

The Saints are currently dealing with injuries at the position to Alvin Kamara (knee), Audric Estime (ankle) and Devin Neal, who left Saturday's preseason matchup against the Los Angeles Rams with another hamstring issue .

While Travis Etienne Jr. is entrenched as the starter, the depth behind him had evaportated, with Kendre Miller one of the last men standing. White is hardly an earth-shattering addition, but he'll provide some needed relief for a position battered by injuries this summer.

The 26-year-old spent his first four seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders, rushing 736 yards and two touchdowns across 45 games while adding 25 catches for 152 yards.

The Saints are also likely to be without rookie first-round pick Jordyn Tyson for the next two months after the wideout suffered a right hamstring injury last week. Not exactly the summer New Orleans would have been hoping for in Kellen Moore's second season.

As for Jones, the former Pro Bowler registered 29 tackles for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last season and has 761 tackles and 12 sacks for his career. The Saints had signed Jones to a one-year deal in early August, though his time in New Orleans only lasted about two weeks.

He'll battle for a reserve linebacker role behind Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw, with Nick Martin and Jaden Dugger currently the frontrunners to earn roster spots and Tatum Bethune, Garret Wallow, Jalen Graham and Luke Gifford on the roster bubble.

articles.title: Re-Ranking Every NHL Team's Prospect Pools After the 2026 Offseason
articles.summary: We know that the Carolina Hurricanes will be the team all 31 other clubs will be aiming for during the 2026-27 campaign.
articles.body:
We know that the Carolina Hurricanes will be the team all 31 other clubs will be aiming for during the 2026-27 campaign.

Which team is best set up for the next few years? Who's set up best for the deepest set of prospects?

Our B/R NHL prospect experts, Adam Herman and Hannah Stuart, voted and ranked all 32 prospect pools ahead of the new season starting next month.

Prospects to Watch: Simas Ignatavičius, Ryder Cali, Jack Devine

Analysis: The Florida Panthers remain in last place, just like last year. Although the team missed the playoffs this past season, they remain clearly determined to extend their window as contenders. This is best evidenced by their big swing for Brady Tkachuk, as well as the addition of Radko Gudas.

While it appears they are likely to return to the playoffs in the near future, the distant future is bleak. In many places, it also echoes the size, physicality, and frustrating nature that the Panthers are prioritizing in their roster players.

Lithuanian winger Simas Ignatavičius is probably their top prospect right now. Coming in at 6'3" and 201 pounds, he's got the size and physicality down easily. He brings solid skating, tenacity, and netfront presence, along with flashes of playmaking. Much of the previous sentence could easily be said about the speedy and physical center Ryder Cali, who doesn't turn 18 until September. Winger Jack Devine doesn't fit the typical physical mold, but he has the tenacity and ability to get to the net. Even Linus Eriksson, whose NHL future I am not convinced of, tends to read more as a support player than a play-driver.

There are clearly traits the Panthers are prioritizing. Perhaps they could prioritize some top-of-the-funnel talent in future drafts? Regardless, these are players who will be useful in their bottom six as they continue to attempt deep playoff runs.

Prospects to Watch: Emil Hemming, Cameron Schmidt, Jakub Vanecek

Analysis: Winger Emil Hemming, a former first-round pick, can look good when he's getting a lot of touches of the puck. In his best moments, he can make things happen in the offensive zone. His skills are not superlative enough to justify the rest of his game, which is inconsistent at the moment. He's not a strong driver of possession, and has some games where he's a non-factor, and he sometimes looks sluggish. As strong as his shot is, it won't matter if he can't do the things that will put him in positions to execute quality chances. Right now, it's a stretch to see him in a top-six role, which means he'll have to rework his game to be more fitting for a checking role. He has the size and tools to make it work.

Cameron Schmidt is exactly the type of gamble worth taking in the third round. The winger is 5'8", but his point production in the WHL in 2025-26 was encouraging: 40 goals and 38 assists in 61 games. He's slippery and clever. He's at his best when he's moving at top speed, as he's able to make plays while in motion. It can be tough for defenders to keep up. He didn't take as big a step as hoped this past season, and he faces an uphill battle to make the NHL because of his size, but there is still a world where he becomes a Jeff Skinner-type player.

Jakub Vanecek is an athletic defenseman. He likes to get involved offensively, although his puck abilities don't necessarily match his ambition. He is an intelligent player who doesn't make many mistakes with the puck and is responsible defensively. The 6'2" defenseman is going to have to transition into more of a shutdown, puck-transporting role at the pro level, but he is cut out for it.

Prospects to Watch: Ike Howard, Samuel Jonsson, Tommy Lafreniere
