articles.title: Could Jed York lose control of the 49ers? Major NFL punishment looms after misdemeanor plea as questions swirl over his future
articles.summary: NFL News: Jed Yorkâs future with the San Francisco 49ers is now under scrutiny after the team owner entered a no contest plea to misdemeanor charges in Ohio. Th.
articles.body: Jed Yorkâs future with the San Francisco 49ers is now under scrutiny after the team owner entered a no contest plea to misdemeanor charges in Ohio. The case has shifted attention from the courtroom to the NFL, which is reviewing the matter under its personal conduct policy. The key question is no longer simply what happened, but how the league could respond to an owner facing criminal penalties.Jed Yorkâs NFL future could depend on league reviewYork pleaded no contest to charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools after his August 23 arrest in East Palestine, Ohio, on suspicion of engaging in prostitution. The plea gives the NFL a clear legal development to examine as it considers whether the incident violates its standards for owners.The league has not announced a punishment. That leaves several possible outcomes, ranging from no disciplinary action to a suspension or other restrictions. A permanent loss of ownership would represent the most serious scenario, and legal experts suggest that such an outcome is far from certain based on the circumstances currently known.Jodi Balsam, a professor of clinical law at Brooklyn Law School and former NFL counsel for operations and litigation, explained how the league typically approaches these cases.âThe typical framework in an incident that comes to the attention of the sports league that might implicate the personal conduct policy is, step one, investigation,â she said. Additionally, she added that leagues can investigate even without a conviction, but a guilty plea removes much of the uncertainty that usually complicates these cases.That investigation could allow the NFL to review police records, court documents and other available evidence before deciding whether York breached the personal conduct policy.What could happen to 49ers owner Jed York?One factor that may matter is cooperation. League investigations can become complicated when facts are disputed or witnesses are unwilling to participate. Balsam noted that this case may present fewer problems on that front.âOften, the biggest hurdle these leagues have is, how do you get people to cooperate and be forthcoming and be truthful,â she said. âThat wonât necessarily be an issue here.âRobert Boland, a sports attorney and professor of sports management and sports law at New York University, also stressed that NFL owners are not outside the reach of the leagueâs personal conduct rules.âOwners are under the personal conduct policy and can be suspended or potentially even separated from the league,â he told Inc.That does not mean York is facing an automatic removal from the 49ers. The NFL will have to determine the appropriate response after reviewing the facts and considering the standards it applies to owners.For now, York remains the principal owner of the 49ers. But the legal case has placed his position in an unusual spotlight, with the league holding the next major decision. Its eventual ruling could have consequences not only for York, but also for how the NFL handles misconduct allegations involving its most powerful stakeholders.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes gets stunning $10B business boost as Whoop investment becomes a major talking point
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has plenty to celebrate away from the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterbackâs early investment in Whoop has gained fresh .
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has plenty to celebrate away from the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterbackâs early investment in Whoop has gained fresh attention after the performance technology company announced a $575 million funding round that lifted its valuation to $10.1 billion. Mahomes backed the company when it was worth about $1.2 billion, making the latest figure a striking reminder of how far that business bet has come.Patrick Mahomesâ Whoop investment gets a huge valuation boostMahomes invested in Whoop in 2020, when the Boston-based company was still establishing itself as one of the most promising names in wearable technology. Its focus was clear: help athletes understand their bodies through data covering sleep, recovery and physical strain.More than five years later, Whoop has grown into a global performance brand. Founder and CEO Will Ahmed announced the new funding on March 31, revealing that the company had raised $575 million at a $10.1 billion valuation.âI am pleased to announce that weâve raised $575M at a $10.1B valuation to accelerate our mission of unlocking human performance and healthspan globally,â Ahmed announced in a statement on X.The funding round was led by Collaborative Fund and included several major investment groups. The company has also attracted an impressive roster of athletes, including Cristiano Ronaldo, LeBron James, Rory McIlroy and Virgil van Dijk.For Mahomes, the connection with Whoop has gone beyond simply owning a stake. He has used the technology himself and has worn the tracker during games. In 2025, he and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, also appeared together in a Whoop campaign built around athletic performance.âPerformance isnât bought. Itâs built.âThat message fits neatly with Mahomesâ own approach to football. His investment also reflects a broader trend among elite athletes who are putting money into companies connected to health, fitness and sports technology.Whoopâs growth adds another win to Mahomesâ business portfolioWhoopâs latest valuation is significant because it shows how dramatically the company has expanded since Mahomes first invested. It now has more than 2.5 million members worldwide and reported positive cash flow for 2025. Subscriptions also increased by 103% during the year.The company operates across roughly 60 countries, with international markets accounting for around 60% of sales. Those numbers suggest Whoop is no longer simply a niche product for professional athletes. Its appeal has widened among consumers who want to monitor recovery and improve everyday performance.Mahomes is also navigating an important period in his football career. After suffering torn ACL and LCL injuries late in the 2025 season, he has been working toward a return for Week 1 of the 2026 campaign.That makes his connection with a recovery-focused company especially notable. While his primary job remains leading the Chiefs, his Whoop investment offers a glimpse into the business instincts developing alongside his NFL career.What began as an early investment in a $1.2 billion startup has now become part of a company valued at $10.1 billion. For Mahomes, it is another reminder that his biggest plays are not always happening on the football field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New Report Concludes At Least 24.5% of NFL Players in Study Had CTE
articles.summary: A new study examining the brains of deceased former NFL players found that at least 24.5 percent of players in its cohort had CTE, a degenerative brain disease.
articles.body:
A new study examining the brains of deceased former NFL players found that at least 24.5 percent of players in its cohort had CTE, a degenerative brain disease.

The study, published by The BMJ , examined the brains of 235 of the 878 former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021. Researchers found 215 of the analyzed brains had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), leading them to the conclusion that at least 24.5 percent of all players who died in that period had CTE.

According to ESPN : "The estimate of 25% is on the 'low end,' said Dr. Daniel Daneshvar, the study's lead author. The study found that the maximum possible prevalence of CTE was around 97%, but the true rate 'is somewhere in the middle,' Daneshvar said."

More broadly, the study incorporated the 1,712 NFL players who died between 2008 and 2021. It found that of 338 former NFL players who donated their brains to be studied for neuropathological evaluation, 315 (93.2 percent) were found to have CTE. The study's main conclusions focused on 2016-2021 because brain donation was most frequent in that period.

Boston University wrote in 2023 that a study of 376 former NFL players showed 345 of them were found to have CTE.

The disease is likely caused by repeated head injuries, leading to the death of nerve cells in the brain. There is currently no way to definitively diagnose CTE in a living person.

Former NFL quarterback Matt Hasselbeck was part of a group that recently went through a series of tests and scans at Boston University that researchers hope will eventually help lead to the ability to diagnose CTE in a living person.

articles.title: New Ashton Jeanty Rumors Reveal Severity of Ankle Injury After Scary Moment at Raiders Practice
articles.summary: After Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty injured his ankle in practice on Sunday, many feared the worst.
articles.body:
After Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty injured his ankle in practice on Sunday, many feared the worst.

However, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Tuesday that Jeanty's outlook isn't so dire, as he avoided any kind of season-ending injury.

"It's nothing like that," Rapoport said. "My understanding... is that it's an ankle sprain believed to be more low than high, and not considered to be a major injury. But it is a real injury, and the reality is, there is a chance that Ashton Jeanty may not be on the field for Week 1. They are hopeful that he will be. There is a chance that he won't be."

Multiple reports sparked a wave of concern on Sunday when it was revealed that Jeanty had to leave practice early and could not put weight on his leg as he was helped off the field by trainers. ESPN's Ryan McFadden reported that the second-year back suffered the injury when he dove for a catch and landed awkwardly on his right leg during team drills, and his teammates "took a knee and said a prayer after Jeanty exited the field."

Jeanty is coming off a strong rookie season. He totaled 266 carries for 975 yards and five touchdowns while also adding 55 receptions for 346 yards and five more scores. The 2025 No. 6 pick was widely expected to make a leap in his sophomore campaign under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak, who was the offensive coordinator of the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

While Jeanty's injury doesn't appear to be a long-term setback, the Raiders will likely be cautious with his recovery. Rapoport noted that his potential absence will allow Las Vegas to explore its running back depth, and "that might not be a bad thing, either." Rookie ball-carrier Mike Washington Jr., a fourth-round pick in this year's draft, has impressed with 119 yards across two preseason games.

Once Jeanty is back at full strength, the Raiders will give him the lion's share of the carries as they try to emerge from their ongoing rebuild.

Along with the four teams from the AFC South, the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings unveiled their new "Rivalries" uniform designs through the "Nike x NFL Rivalries" program on Tuesday. Each team will debut its uniform during a home game against its division rival this year.

"Revealing eight new Rivalries uniforms marks the next chapter in a program that is beloved by fans across the NFL and Nike," Taryn Hutt, vice president of club marketing for the NFL, said in a statement, per Scott Thompson of Fox News. "By spotlighting the launch of the AFC South and NFC North Clubs and the passionate communities behind them, we continue to capture the spirit and tradition of football's greatest divisional rivalries."

The Packers will be the first to showcase their Rivalries uniforms when they face the Bears in Week 5. The Lions will follow in Week 8 against the Vikings, who will then show off their new threads against Detroit in Week 15. Chicago will rock the new uniforms in Week 16 against Green Bay.

The Rivalries uniforms will be added to each team's alternate jersey lineup for the next three years. The teams that had their Rivalries uniforms debut last year will also wear them at some point this season, and it can be expected that more teams will join the program in 2027 and 2028.

articles.summary: The four teams in the AFC South have unveiled the "rivalries" uniforms they will use for one divisional game during the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
The four teams in the AFC South have unveiled the "rivalries" uniforms they will use for one divisional game during the 2026 NFL season.

Nike and the NFL dropped the special uniforms for the Indianapolis Colts, Houston Texans, Jacksonville Jaguars and Tennessee Titans.

The Colts will be the first AFC South team to wear their new rivalries uniform on Sept. 27 when they host the Houston Texans at Lucas Oil Stadium.

Jacksonville will go second when it dons its new threads against the Colts in Week 8, followed by the Titans when they host the Jaguars in Week 10.

The Texans will be the final AFC South team to showcase their rivalries look when they wear it against Indianapolis in Week 11 on Thursday Night Football.

This marks the second year of the "rivalries" uniforms for the NFL. They are "rooted extensively in the legacies and inspirations true to each team." The AFC East and NFC West got first dibs during the 2025 season.

Unlike the traditional alternate uniforms all 32 teams will use in rotation, the rivalries look is being phased into the NFL over a period of four years. The NFC East and AFC West will get theirs in 2027, followed by the AFC North and NFC South in 2028.

The NFL will keep the rivalry uniforms in rotation for three years after their debut. So the AFC South will use these particular jerseys through the 2028 campaign.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Not Playing in Browns' Preseason Finale Explained by Todd Monken After QB1 Snub
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Tuesday that Shedeur Sanders won't play in the team's preseason finale on Thursday, saying they want to give extended playing time to Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters on Tuesday that Shedeur Sanders won't play in the team's preseason finale on Thursday, saying they want to give extended playing time to Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green.

Monken also said that Deshaun Watson was the clear frontrunner for the starting position in the spring but Sanders made it a competition with his play over the summer.

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

Watson was officially, and somewhat shockingly , named the team's starter on Monday.

Neither Watson or Sanders were exactly brilliant during the first two preseason games:

But history suggests that Watson has little room for growth. Since joining the Browns in 2022 he's thrown for 3,365 yards, 19 touchdowns and 12 interceptions across 19 games, taking 70 sacks while completing 61.2 percent of his passes. The Browns are 9-10 in his starts.

Sanders is more of an unknown, though his rookie season was rough after he threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games (seven starts), taking 23 sacks while completing just 56.6 percent of his passes. The Browns went 3-4 in his starts.

One line of thinking is that the Browns probably should determine once and for all what they have in Sanders, especially since they have two first-round picks ahead of the 2027 draft, which is expected to have a strong quarterback class. It's hard to do that when he's sitting on the bench.

But Monken is a first-year head coach who wants to make a strong initial impression, and picking the veteran quarterback is normally the safer bet. The issue in this case is that Watson has never been good in Cleveland and was awful in his second preseason appearance. Choosing him as the starter certainly feels like a predetermined choice.

Regardless, the pecking order has been set. Nobody will be surprised if Sanders ultimately takes over as the starter at some point in the regular season, however.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors Reveal Haason Reddick Interest After Von Miller's Cowboys Contract
articles.summary: Veteran outside linebacker Haason Reddick is receiving interest from NFL teams amid franchises inking deals with pass-rushers, including the Dallas Cowboys' one-year deal for Von Miller.
articles.body:
Veteran outside linebacker Haason Reddick is receiving interest from NFL teams amid franchises inking deals with pass-rushers, including the Dallas Cowboys' one-year deal for Von Miller.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the latest.

Reddick has played nine NFL seasons for the Arizona Cardinals, Carolina Panthers, Philadelphia Eagles, New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He is a two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro Second Teamer who amassed 50.5 sacks from 2020-2023.

Reddick, who turns 32 on Sept. 22, has not been as productive in recent years. He amassed one sack and three quarterback hits over 10 games on the 2024 Jets and 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hits in 13 games for the 2025 Buccaneers.

Still, there's no denying his talent, and it's certainly possible Reddick can enjoy a resurgence in 2026. Teams reportedly have interest in bringing him aboard, so we'll see if anything comes to fruition before Week 1 of the NFL season, which runs from Sept. 9-14.

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase Injury Update, Latest on Bengals WR's Status After Apparent Leg Issue at Practice
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase appears to have avoided a serious left leg injury during his team's practice on Tuesday, as he said that he would've been able to continue if needed after suffering a "hyperextension."
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase appears to have avoided a serious left leg injury during his team's practice on Tuesday, as he said that he would've been able to continue if needed after suffering a "hyperextension."

CBS Cincinnati's Yanni Tragellis and NBC 5 Cincinnati's Charlie Clifford provided more information.

The former LSU star has posted a 17-game average of 113 catches, 1,490 yards and 12 touchdowns over his first five seasons (2021-2025), per Pro Football Reference .

Chase enjoyed a career-best 2024 season, winning the receiver triple crown with 127 catches, 1,708 yards and 17 touchdowns, leading pass-catchers in all categories. For his efforts, Chase earned himself a four-year, $161 million contract extension .

Chase was exceptional yet again in 2025, catching 125 passes for 1,412 yards and eight scores. He's put up those numbers despite the team missing superstar quarterback Joe Burrow, who was out nine weeks after suffering a Grade 3 turf toe injury a Week 2 win (31-27) against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: New Giants Rumors Update Calvin Austin III's 'Serious' Knee Injury Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The New York Giants are hoping for the best after a key member of the offense suffered an injury on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are hoping for the best after a key member of the offense suffered an injury on Tuesday.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, wide receiver Calvin Austin suffered a "serious knee injury" and had to be carted off the field during practice.

According to Dan Duggan of The Athletic, Austin was running a route in 1-on-1s when he went down with what appeared to be a right knee injury. Duggan noted that those around Austin "couldn't even look" as he was attended to.

The injury comes ahead of Austin's fifth NFL season, where he was looking to break through as a top option in New York. He spent the first four years of his career with the Pittsburgh Steelers before signing with the Giants in March.

Last year, Austin recorded 372 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games.

Austin was expected to be the starting slot receiver for the Giants this year, but his injury on Tuesday means New York might have to find someone else to fill that role in the meantime. With Malik Nabers and Darius Slayton starting on the outside, the Giants could pivot to Braxton Berrios in the slot.

With Odell Beckham Jr. still looking for a permanent spot on the Giants, the veteran receiver could be in the mix to take over Austin's role.

Unfortunately for Austin, a significant injury would only add to what has been an injury-filled start to his career. Drafted in the fourth round in 2022, he missed all of his rookie season because of a lingering foot injury that he suffered in training camp.

articles.title: How Odell Beckham Jr., Giants Depth Chart Are Impacted by Austin Injury Ahead of Roster Cut Deadline
articles.summary: The New York Giants' receiving corps took a hit after Calvin Austin III suffered an injury in practice on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The New York Giants' receiving corps took a hit after Calvin Austin III suffered an injury in practice on Tuesday.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Austin was carted off the field after a "serious" knee injury.

With the 27-year-old likely set to miss time, the Giants will look further down their depth chart as they attempt to make up for his impact.

This could be beneficial for Odell Beckham Jr.'s chances of making the team, as the veteran is looking to stay in New York beyond Sunday's deadline to trim rosters down to 53 players.

Paul Schwartz of the New York Post also noted that Austin's injury "opens the door" for Beckham to secure a roster spot.

Although Beckham didn't play for any team during the 2025 season, he returned to the squad that he started his career with on a minimum contract in June.

The 33-year-old has been on the Giants' roster bubble throughout training camp, with Charlotte Carroll of The Athletic predicting that he wouldn't make the team on Monday.

While Beckham has occasionally worked with New York's first-team offense, he's spent the majority of camp as a reserve option. Still, he's made several impressive plays in practice.

During his first preseason appearance this year, he caught two passes for six yards. In Beckham's second preseason contest, he hauled in two receptions for 17 yards.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh was particularly impressed with his latest performance.

"I thought he looked pretty good," Harbaugh said, per Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News . "He made a couple catches. There were some things he could have done better. But he looked solid, I would say. I love Odell. What he's doing, what he's fighting for, I don't know how it's gonna turn out … But to see his fight, his determination, his humility … [I'm] really proud of him."

Malik Nabers and Darius Slayton are New York's established starters at wide receiver, while Malachi Fields was selected with a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL draft. The Giants also brought in Darnell Mooney on a one-year deal worth up to $10 million in March.

Braxton Berrios, Dalen Cambre, Xavier Gipson, Isaiah Hodgins and Jalin Hyatt are among the players competing with Beckham for New York's backup receiver spots.

Sunday's cut-down deadline is at 6 p.m. ET.

articles.title: NFL Injury News: Ja'Marr Chase hurt his knee, left practice; here's the latest update
articles.summary: NFL News: For about twelve hours, Bengals fans lived through the exact nightmare scenario nobody wants three weeks before kickoff. Their $161 million receiver, .
articles.body: For about twelve hours, Bengals fans lived through the exact nightmare scenario nobody wants three weeks before kickoff. Their $161 million receiver, the guy the entire offense runs through, went down on a routine practice rep with no contact, no pileup, just a bad landing, and grabbed his knee as it mattered. In a league where careers and playoff hopes turn on exactly this kind of moment, that clip was enough to send an entire fanbase into a spiral before a single official word came out. Then, just as fast as the panic built, Chase himself picked up a mic and tried to shut it all down. Here's the full arc, from scare to relief, and why it's still worth reading the fine print.JaâMarr Chaseâs scary injury had Bengals fans fearing the worst Chase went up for a deep route against teammate DJ Turner at Tuesday's practice, landed awkwardly, and immediately grabbed his left knee. Video of the moment spread fast, Chase limping, trainers rushing over, head athletic trainer Matt Summers examining him for several minutes on the field.For a team about to open its season, and a receiver who just signed a four-year, $161 million extension in March, that's the kind of clip that sends fanbases spiraling before anyone's said a word officially.Here's the thing, even in the moment, this didn't look like a disaster. Chase walked off under his own power. His limp reportedly eased up as the day went on. He stayed on the practice field afterward instead of heading straight to the locker room, and was seen casually talking with Joe Burrow and DJ Turner not long after. None of that screams "serious injury." But screenshots of a guy grabbing his knee travel faster than context does, so the panic had already set in online before those details caught up.Chase himself is saying it's nothingSpeaking on ESPN 1530 with Tony Pike and Mo Egger, Chase called it a mild hyperextension and said he could have kept playing if it had been a real game. Straight from the source, that's about as reassuring as it gets.That said, worth flagging that this is Chase's own read on his own knee, on a radio hit, not an official Bengals medical statement or an MRI result. Players downplay injuries all the time, sometimes because that's genuinely how it feels, sometimes because nobody wants to hand the rest of the league bulletin-board material before Week 1. The Bengals themselves haven't put out an official statement on severity, so until there's a practice report or a coach's presser confirming Chase is full-go, "hyperextension, no big deal" is Chase's word, not a diagnosis.Best case: this really was a scare and nothing more, and Chase is back to full practice reps within days. Worst case: hyperextensions can still linger even when a guy insists he's fine. Bengals fans have been burned by exactly this pattern before with Chase's past hip and shoulder injuries, where "day-to-day" turned into multiple missed games. For now, take the good news, but keep one eye on the practice report before fully exhaling.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: The fragile, shaky, not-yet-feelgood story of Tua Tagovailoa's next act
articles.summary: Atlanta has two quarterbacks and one big problem: Can either stay healthy?
articles.body:
Walk very gently around the Falcons ' practice fields in Flowery Branch, Georgia. You might injure a quarterback.

Yes, while Cleveland is the site of the most controversial and misbegotten quarterback situation , Atlanta is home to the most delicate. Two oft-injured quarterbacks, Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., are ever-so-carefully competing for the starting job like they're trying to run across a hockey rink.

Penix, who partially tore his ACL last November, finally received clearance to begin full 11-on-11 work on Monday, meaning the Falcons' QB competition can now begin in earnest. Good thing, too, because the regular-season opener is coming up fast, and it's probably a good idea to have a starting QB in place at that point.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

The Falcons snagged Tagovailoa for the NFL equivalent of a scratch-and-dent bargain — one year, $1.2 million — as a combination insurance policy/camp challenge for Penix. This marks a clear new chapter for Tagovailoa, who first came to prominence at Alabama, throwing the famous second-and-26 national championship-winning pass against Georgia in the same building the Falcons call home. After going to Miami in the pandemic draft, where he sported a spectacular suit in his parents' home, Tagovailoa strung together six occasionally transcendent, often maddening injury-pocked seasons.

Tagovailoa occupies a strangely sympathetic position in the modern NFL. No other quarterback has suffered so much, so visibly in this decade, with at least four documented head injuries, along with an assortment of other health woes. A not-insignificant contingent of NFL fandom and commentators has called on Tagovailoa to retire — not because he's hurting the team, which is usually the reason for these calls, but out of fear he's hurting himself and jeopardizing his future.

A newly-released study which states that 25 percent of recently deceased NFL players had CTE is a stark reminder that head trauma remains a concern for NFL players, if not necessarily a headline-worthy news item. And if you're making a list of known head trauma victims now playing in the NFL, well, Tagovailoa tops the list, and there's no close second.

The head injuries alone are enough to proceed with caution on Tagovailoa, but this is a guy who's sustained shots all over his body — back, shoulder, knee, hip, ankle, throwing hand, foot, ribs. Point to a spot between the top of your head and the soles of your feet, and Tagovailoa has probably lost games after injuring it. He's been carted off fields all over the country, wearing both Alabama crimson and Miami teal. Even though he's now in Falcon red-and-black, the questions persist: How much more can he take of this?

For his part, Tagovailoa leans heavily on his faith to guide him through one of the more agonizing journeys in the NFL right now. "Outside of being able to feel centered, it also gives me a lot of perspective on life, what's important in life," he said recently at training camp. "Football is just what we do. It's not who we are."

After missing time early in the preseason with a tight back, Tagovailoa has been taking first-team reps while Penix heals. The results have looked good in practice, not so good in the first preseason game against Denver — 3-for-5 for 22 yards, with just one first down in two offensive series. He's never had a big arm, and he hasn't unleashed it with any regularity in a Falcons uniform, either.

"You have to make use of every opportunity you have, and that's not what we did," Tagovailoa said after the Broncos game, via The Athletic . "Definitely not up to standard. I have to be better for our guys."

"He's getting better every day," Falcons quarterbacks coach Alex Van Pelt insisted recently, per the team's website . "I think he's becoming more comfortable with the system and the play-calls and protection adjustments and everything."

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski is keeping his cards close on naming a starter, waiting to see how Penix performs in full-squad drills. But as with the ongoing scuffle in Cleveland, the fact that Tagovailoa hasn't yet seized the job for himself is at least a mild indictment in itself. (Tagovailoa did not play in the Falcons' second preseason game; no starters did.)

NFL news, live updates: Ja'Marr Chase 'fine' after 'little hyperextension' of his knee; Browns announce Deshaun Watson as starter over Shedeur Sanders

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest

The Falcons backed themselves into this corner by drafting Penix just weeks after signing now-departed Kirk Cousins , and then watching as both went down with injuries and ineffectiveness. What should have been a position of excessive riches is now one of the largest question marks in the NFL.

For a team that's suffering through the longest playoff drought outside of the Jets — eight years and counting — the Falcons can't afford any more question marks. Atlanta needs answers, and fast. Still undetermined: whether Tagovailoa is the one to provide them.

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan breaks 49ers silence on Jed York arrest, says he still has 'respect' for the club owner
articles.summary: Kyle Shanahan says Jed York's arrest in an Ohio prostitution sting has no effect on the San Francisco 49ers as a team heading into the season.
articles.body: The San Francisco 49ers said they weren't going to comment about owner Jed York getting caught up in a prostitution sting over the weekend because the legal matter is closed , but that policy collapsed in coach Kyle Shanahan's first press conference since the incident. Shanahan became the first 49ers official to face questions, and he felt obliged to provide answers. (Dude is a saint). Shanahan said York's arrest and ensuing no-contest plea to misdemeanor disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools charges in a deal with an Ohio prosecutor has no effect on the Bay Area football team. MORE DETAILS EMERGE ABOUT JED YORK'S ARREST IN PROSTITUTION STING "My view is, as the coach, does it have effect on us as a team?" Shanahan said. "And that's what I continue to answer on from a football standpoint. It has no effect on us. I mean, as far as what we do day to day, what we talk about, it hasn't been mentioned in a meeting today. It doesn't have to do with what happens on the field." Shanahan, who was involved in a head-on collision in July that affected how much he was on the field early in training camp, doesn't believe that or York's legal trouble will distract the football team in the upcoming season. "Well, the one thing that went on yesterday I don't think pertained to our players much," Shanahan said. "And if you guys talk about me getting in a car accident, I think that's kind of a joke that people think that's a distraction to our team. "So I think it's been training camp as usual." 49ERS COACH KYLE SHANAHAN ADMITS HE CAUSED CAR CRASH AFTER TAKING EYES OFF ROAD TO FIND HIS PHONE This, of course, is a head coach's spin on an uncomfortable situation. The majority owner of the team spent a day in jail and was splashed across national headlines because, police documents say, he went on a website in Ohio and tried to enlist the services of a prostitute on Sunday. Three times. And he got caught because what he was actually doing was connecting with an operation run by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, which arrested him with the help of East Palestine police. NFL EMPLOYEES’ TROUBLING DRIVING INCIDENTS MOUNT, COSTING JOBS AND PUTTING OTHERS AT RISK Despite those details, Shanahan said he has not changed his opinion about the club's owner or his family. "Obviously, it's a very tough situation," Shanahan admitted after saying he has spoken to York the last two days. "I mean, the views for the organization going forward is the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that. "But I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got a lot of respect for Danielle. Their family does mean a lot to me. So I'm like, you know, with it being a personal [matter], I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way." Danielle Belluomini is York's wife of 15 years, but even the marriage has become a newsworthy drama. Multiple reports have cited a divorce petition filed by York almost four months ago with the reason for the break being "irreconcilable differences." NFL owners are scheduled to gather on Wednesday to vote on the sale of the Seattle Seahawks and the York situation will almost definitely be discussed in some capacity. The league released a statement on Monday saying it is aware of York's situation, and he is subject to discipline under its Personal Conduct Policy. So, whether Shanahan admits it or not, the football team could be affected if York is disciplined and that rises to a suspension or even removal — the latter of which is not likely but cannot be ruled out. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP None of that is a concern right now for the coach, and he believes his players aren't moved by the publicity of York's troubles. "That's what these guys deal with their whole careers," Shanahan said. "I got cameras on all the time. They got cameras in their face right after games, when they're not feeling right or something very emotional could have happened. "I feel something like this is actually easier for them than some of the stuff they have to deal with in the heat of battle of things that are more personal to themselves." The majority owner of the team spent a day in jail and was splashed across national headlines because, police documents say, he went on a website in Ohio and tried to enlist the services of a prostitute on Sunday. Three times. And he got caught because what he was actually doing was connecting with an operation run by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, which arrested him with the help of East Palestine police. NFL EMPLOYEES’ TROUBLING DRIVING INCIDENTS MOUNT, COSTING JOBS AND PUTTING OTHERS AT RISK Despite those details, Shanahan said he has not changed his opinion about the club's owner or his family. "Obviously, it's a very tough situation," Shanahan admitted after saying he has spoken to York the last two days. "I mean, the views for the organization going forward is the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that. "But I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got a lot of respect for Danielle. Their family does mean a lot to me. So I'm like, you know, with it being a personal [matter], I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way." Danielle Belluomini is York's wife of 15 years, but even the marriage has become a newsworthy drama. Multiple reports have cited a divorce petition filed by York almost four months ago with the reason for the break being "irreconcilable differences." NFL owners are scheduled to gather on Wednesday to vote on the sale of the Seattle Seahawks and the York situation will almost definitely be discussed in some capacity. The league released a statement on Monday saying it is aware of York's situation, and he is subject to discipline under its Personal Conduct Policy. So, whether Shanahan admits it or not, the football team could be affected if York is disciplined and that rises to a suspension or even removal — the latter of which is not likely but cannot be ruled out. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP None of that is a concern right now for the coach, and he believes his players aren't moved by the publicity of York's troubles. "That's what these guys deal with their whole careers," Shanahan said. "I got cameras on all the time. They got cameras in their face right after games, when they're not feeling right or something very emotional could have happened. "I feel something like this is actually easier for them than some of the stuff they have to deal with in the heat of battle of things that are more personal to themselves." articles.title: 49ers owner Jed York reportedly contacted fictitious prostitution ad posted by police prior to arrest
articles.summary: York pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges, disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools, was sentenced to two days in jail and fined $1,150.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used the pseudonym "Joe" while responding to a fictitious ad on a prostitution website, leading to his Sunday morning arrest in a mobile home park located in East Palestine, Ohio, according to a Tuesday report from The Athletic .

York was charged with a pair of misdemeanors, initially including a prostitution charge that was eventually amended to disorderly conduct through a plea agreement, per ESPN . York's other charge was reportedly for possession of criminal tools, a classification that can apply to a cell phone. He pleaded no contest, was sentenced to two days in jail, one for each charge, and fined $1,150.

The Athletic, citing an incident report from the Mahoning Valley Law Enforcement Task Force, reported that police deployed an undercover advertisement, masquerading as a woman, to arrange a meeting with the 46-year-old York, who reportedly filed for divorce from his wife in May.

York contacted what he didn't know was an undercover officer twice on Saturday, according to ESPN , which also cited the incident report. The undercover officer reportedly didn't respond to York until Sunday, when York sent a third message.

York, a Youngstown, Ohio, native, messaged at 9:11 a.m. ET that he was driving in from nearby Boardman, per The Athletic. The two sides reportedly agreed on one hour of "full service sexual activity" for $160, and York was provided a fake lot number in East Palestine mobile home park, identified as the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in ESPN's report.

As reported by The Athletic, York was seen driving a rental car into the mobile home park and then back out to the main road after he couldn't find the made-up lot number. That's where he was reportedly stopped by police, who took York's phone and the $160 he planned to pay. That money was ultimately forfeited to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, according to The Athletic's report, but York's phone was returned.

NFL news, live updates: Ja'Marr Chase 'fine' after 'little hyperextension' of his knee; Browns announce Deshaun Watson as starter over Shedeur Sanders

Sean McVay can't comprehend players going from NFL camps back to college: 'I feel like I took a freakin' gummy'

At least 25% of ex-NFL players who died from 2016-2021 had CTE, according to new study; NFLPA says findings should be 'a call to action across the entire football ecosystem'

York was named the 49ers' CEO in 2008. That's when he assumed day-to-day control of the team from his parents. In 2024, he purchased enough equity from his family to take over as the organization's principal owner.

Under York's supervision, San Francisco has reached the Super Bowl three times, although the franchise is still searching for its first ring since the 1994 season.

"As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time," the 49ers said in a statement regarding York's arrest.

The incident will be reviewed under the NFL's personal conduct policy, a league spokesperson said in a statement, according to multiple outlets.

Notably, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft didn't face punishment from the NFL after he was accused of paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. However, the charges against Kraft, misdemeanor counts of soliciting prostitution, were dropped.

articles.title: 49ers Owner Jed York Texted Woman He Believed Was a Prostitute Before His Arrest in Police Sting
articles.summary: SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used an alias when he sent text messages over two days to a woman he believed to be a prostitute before he was arrested in a sting operation in Ohio, according to a police incident report obtained Tuesday.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York used an alias when he sent text messages over two days to a woman he believed to be a prostitute before he was arrested in a sting operation in Ohio, according to a police incident report obtained Tuesday.

The report from the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force had more than two pages redacted but provided more details about what led to York's arrest and ultimately to him pleading no contest Monday to two misdemeanors.

York initially responded to an advertisement placed by police on a known prostitution website on Saturday, according to the report, sending two messages that went unanswered and saying his name was "Joe" and that he wanted to visit the woman.

49ers Owner Pleads No Contest to Misdemeanor Charges (AP)

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

York texted again Sunday morning and said he wanted to see the woman. He said he was staying nearby and asked for her address. He asked how much the woman charged and was told it was $160 for "full service sexual activity," the report said.

York took a rental car to a mobile home park in East Palestine, Ohio, where he was given a fictitious lot number. He texted when he arrived at the mobile home park. He was then directed back to the main road, where he was stopped by marked police units. Police found York had $160 that was seized and they sent a text to his phone to determine it was the same one used to arrange the meeting.

He was booked into jail and was released after posting a $5,000 bond. York was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He pleaded no contest Monday to that charge and to possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to the ad.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. The $160 that was seized from him was given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course.

York has been in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown, for most of the summer. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records.

The NFL issued a statement saying the league is aware of the arrest and will review it under the personal conduct policy. Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the policy.

The team said that the "legal matter" had been resolved and that it would have no additional comment.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said Tuesday that he has talked to York the past two days and doesn't believe the arrest will have any impact on the team.

"Obviously, it's a very tough situation," Shanahan said. "The views for the organization going forward are the same as usual. There won't be any difference in that. But I know it's extremely fresh. I think it's a very, very personal situation. I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got lot of respect for Danielle. The family does mean a lot to me. With it being this personal, I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way."

Shanahan said he doesn't expect any change in York's involvement with the team, saying he has always allowed Shanahan and general manager John Lynch to make the football decisions.

Shanahan said he doesn't feel the need to address the situation with his players.

Star linebacker Fred Warner said the players were aware of it but that he didn't believe it would be a distraction.

"We all have social media, so we see things," he said. "But at the same time, I got a lot of love, a lot respect for Jed, and don't feel the need to comment on the situation. I think the team is kind of the same way. It really wasn't a conversation being had in the locker room. Of course, yeah, you notice it, but at the time, we were so hyper-focused in this building of trying to prepare for Week 1. A lot of guys are on the bubble trying to make the team. So we're just trying to get better as a football team and that's a personal situation, and letting it stay personal with him."

articles.title: Big Ten passes rule banning NFL players from returning
articles.summary: A fan-favorite will not be able to return to Illinois this fall.
articles.body:
The Big Ten announced a ruling Tuesday morning that would ban players returning from the NFL to play for a Big Ten school.

Sources: The Big Ten is set to pass a rule today that doesn’t allow players to return from the NFL and play for a Big Ten school. Anyone who has declared for the NFL Draft and did not withdraw, appeared on an NFL roster or signed a contract with a pro league cannot be on a Big… — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) August 25, 2026

Sources: The Big Ten is set to pass a rule today that doesn’t allow players to return from the NFL and play for a Big Ten school. Anyone who has declared for the NFL Draft and did not withdraw, appeared on an NFL roster or signed a contract with a pro league cannot be on a Big…

The ruling comes after Dae'Quan Wright, a tight end for the Cleveland Browns , announced his intentions to leave the NFL and join his previous head coach from a year ago, Lane Kiffin, at LSU.

While college basketball has seen its fair share of similar instances, this was the first case in college football, with many more likely to pursue the option to return to college.

Although the Big Ten has been the first conference to ban former NFL players from playing in their conference, there is an expectation that the SEC will have similar talks regarding a ruling.

Following comments made by Bret Bielema last week, this could have notable repercussions for Illinois.

Former Illini wide receiver Hank Beatty and offensive lineman Melvin Priestly were prime candidates to return prior to the ruling.

Bielema had mentioned an interest in recruiting them to return to Illinois if both were eligible.

Both would have been great additions to the roster this fall, but as it stands, the Illinois roster appears to be set ahead of its season opener on September 3rd against UAB.

At a time when college athletics is akin to the Wild West, a ruling such as this provides a rare win for the NCAA to create a more stable league.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy open to keeping four quarterbacks
articles.summary: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy open to keeping four QBs.
articles.body:
Mike McCarthy is not opposed to an unusually crowded quarterback room.

In fact, the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach believes keeping four quarterbacks could provide a meaningful benefit once the regular season begins, particularly given the depth and experience Pittsburgh has assembled at the position.

"I'd take six QBs in the building if it worked," McCarthy said via Mike DeFabo .

McCarthy's comments come as the Steelers evaluate their quarterback situation heading into the final stages of the preseason. Pittsburgh currently has four quarterbacks competing for roster spots: veteran Aaron Rodgers , Mason Rudolph , rookie Drew Allar and second-year quarterback Will Howard .

While most NFL teams typically carry three quarterbacks on their active roster, McCarthy indicated that the Steelers could consider keeping all four if the roster construction allows for it.

"If you have four quarterbacks in that room, especially given the quality that we have, I think it only enhances what the regular season would look like," McCarthy said.

“I’d keep six QBs in the building if it worked.” Mike McCarthy dismissed the notion that keeping four QBs would take away opportunities to develop the young passers. pic.twitter.com/alWS7XNWhj — Mike DeFabo (@MikeDeFabo) August 25, 2026

“I’d keep six QBs in the building if it worked.” Mike McCarthy dismissed the notion that keeping four QBs would take away opportunities to develop the young passers. pic.twitter.com/alWS7XNWhj

The Steelers have invested in developing the position, with Allar selected in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft and Howard entering his second season after being selected in the sixth round last year. Rudolph, meanwhile, provides significant NFL experience behind Rodgers.

The potential value of carrying four quarterbacks extends beyond simply having an additional player available on game day. McCarthy believes the competition and preparation within the room can benefit the entire offense throughout the season.

That philosophy also applies to Pittsburgh's quarterback development program.

McCarthy said his quarterback school could "kick up some" once the regular season arrives because the quarterbacks will no longer be working under the same time constraints that exist during training camp practices.

The additional time could allow the Steelers to devote more attention to the finer details of the position, including preparation, communication, film study and offensive concepts.

For a team with a veteran starter in Rodgers and two young quarterbacks in Allar and Howard, that extra developmental work could prove valuable.

The Steelers also have Rudolph, who has experience in Pittsburgh's system and has started games during his NFL career. Keeping all four would give McCarthy a veteran presence behind Rodgers while allowing the organization to continue developing its two younger quarterbacks.

Ultimately, the decision will come down to roster mathematics and how the Steelers believe they can best allocate their available spots.

articles.title: Giants Reportedly Trade OL to Chiefs Ahead of 2026 NFL Season, Full Return Revealed
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs reportedly are bolstering their offensive line before the start of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs reportedly are bolstering their offensive line before the start of the 2026 NFL season.

Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the team traded a 2028 seventh-round pick to the New York Giants in return for guard Joshua Ezeudu.

Ezeudu was a third-round pick in 2022 out of North Carolina and spent each season of his NFL career with the Giants. He appeared in 33 games with New York, starting seven at left tackle, two at left guard and one as an extra lineman.

Unfortunately, injuries have plagued the early part of Ezeudu's career, as he missed a good portion of the 2023 season before missing all of the 2025 campaign with a calf injury.

Ezeudu has also been dealing with an injury in training camp, but head coach John Harbaugh described it as not "a long-term injury." Harbaugh had also recently switched Ezeudu to right guard after spending most of his time at tackle over the last few seasons.

"The position flex is the idea. You may have noticed he went back out to tackle in the fourth quarter, so the ability for him to play both guard and tackle, particularly on the right side, would be helpful for us, and that's our thought," Harbaugh told reporters this week. "He's kind of getting to the point now where we feel like he could swing, right tackle, right guard."

How the Chiefs plan to use Ezeudu remains to be seen, but they clearly felt their offensive line needed more depth as it looks to protect Patrick Mahomes following last year's season-ending injury.
